result.label: G05-nfl-core-model
result.summary: This group is the NFL spread/total forecast core: nfl-pbp.js streams nflverse play-by-play into per-team-week JSON feature blobs; nfl-ensemble.js aggregates those (recency-weighted, strictly week < target) into 31 component models, calibrates feature-differential slopes on seasons before 2022, grades every component walk-forward and weights by exp(-0.7*RMSE), then blends. Market data enters through game_lines.spread/total, which for every completed game is the closing line (games() hard-codes NULL AS open_spread at nfl-ensemble.js:60), so market_anchor and market_regression are graded against the close, get the lowest RMSE, and dominate the raw blend; the memory claim "model ≈ 0.68 + 0.632·market" is the measured consequence, not a constant in code. Production consumers (nfl-auto-picks.js:83, nfl-unified-engine.js:39) use blendMode market_residual, which returns exactly the market unless a component clears the residual gate (n>=250, gain>=0.03, t<=-1.645). Lookahead audit: featureAggregates, scheduleFaced (C04), weekly-feature-store, spread-context, gbm priorMean, qbr and preseason-blend are all cutoff-safe; three chronology holes remain — calibration slopes fit on 2015-2021 are reused to grade 2018-2021 games in the weight fit (in-sample, contradicts the docstring and the C07 text), nfl-roster-strength overlays the live roster onto any current-season week, and nfl-scheme's validateSchemeAdjustment gates on a flag built from the test season's full-season features. Codex M01 is verified fixed at nfl-preseason-blend.js:321 (weightOnPrior = sigma²/(sigma²+n·tau²)), but that module and nfl-team-strength.js are imported only by tests. One real metric bug: team-level pass attempts include sacks (nfl-pbp.js:274), biasing completion_pct, explosive_pass_rate, int_rate and adot low and feeding one challenger component. nfl-weekly-state.js does not exist; the name refers to nfl-weekly-feature-store.js. Overall the pipeline is structurally sound walk-forward research code whose only production authority is "return the market"; the defects found are P2 chronology/metric issues plus hygiene, nothing that changes money today.

result.label: G02-migrations-late
result.summary: Migrations 018-035 add the late-2026 evidence layer: saved prop tickets, typed news events, the Decision Inbox, quote-tape indexes, the Scottfree research panel, the execution lifecycle ledger (with fill_confirmed pinned to 0), candidate findings, the append-only decision tape with observation identity, settlement corrections, the quote receipt clock, push probability, the T-60 runner ledger, and alt-spread capture with a trigger fence protecting nfl_teaser_price_ledger. All are wired through server/db/migrate.js (filename-sorted, one transaction per file, preflight repairs and a VACUUM INTO snapshot before the first pending file); the live DB holds all 35 schema_migrations rows (000-029, 031-035) and every trigger these files install. The C03 fix is verified: 027 refuses in-transaction when lifecycle events exist (027:148-154) and server/db/preflight.js performs the parent rebuild outside any transaction with foreign keys actually suspended; 031 and 032 lift and restore their append-only triggers around their backfills (031:148/167-171, 032:92/99-103), and test/migration-027-populated-upgrade.test.js now seeds runs and batches so both backfills execute under test. Migration 030 is a reserved-then-abandoned number (CODEX-6-HANDOFF.md:157-158), not a gap in applied history, but a future 030_* file would order differently on fresh vs existing installs. The one P1 is at the producer boundary rather than in the migration: 032 introduced the receipt clock and promised new captures would carry it, yet the two live producers (book-feeds.js:417, line-shopping.js:66) never pass receivedAt, so all 346 batches captured since 032 (including the TNF T-60 window) are labelled legacy_request_time_only and nfl-t60-packet.js:214-216 can grant no prospective received_by_cutoff quote; the T-60 experiment is structurally empty. Secondary: rollbacks take no snapshot and 018-024 down() drop populated tables without refusal; the frozen baseline schema has been retro-edited to include 029's index and 032's columns but not other migrations' objects; scripts/migrate.mjs runs a whole-DB foreign_key_check after commit. Structure is acceptable: the migration code is careful and well-documented, the defects are in surrounding wiring and hygiene.

result.label: G01-platform-db
result.summary: This group is the boot spine of Gridiron HQ: server/index.js guards port 5177, dynamically imports db/index.js (opens server/data.sqlite, sets PRAGMAs, applies the frozen 000_legacy_schema assembled from four schema fragments, runs a daily quick_check, copies the legacy espn_settings row), awaits runMigrations() (preflight repair, one VACUUM INTO snapshot, then 001-035 in filename order, each in BEGIN IMMEDIATE), imports 30 routers, runs seedIfEmpty() on every boot, starts the scheduler and draft clock, mounts routes, and listens on 127.0.0.1. Auth is bearer-token sha256 against auth_sessions/users with league_memberships, draft_team_ownership and model_permissions as authorization sources; legacy-access.js wraps only five route families plus /api/dev at mount level. The four schema fragments are consistent with their manifests (54/65/45/51 tables, all indexes/triggers matched programmatically) except that nfl-n-to-z.js was edited twice after the FROZEN declaration (received_at/receipt_clock_source columns and idx_nfl_quote_commence, both 2026-09-10) without updating the manifest. The protected-table pattern (BEFORE UPDATE/DELETE RAISE(ABORT) pairs, guards lifted and restored inside backfill migrations) is applied consistently; preflight.js exists precisely because 027 would cascade into an append-only child, and it has never had to fire on the live DB. The 000_legacy_schema row sitting after 017 in schema_migrations is the designed upgrade path, not a fault: db/index.js applies it at open when unrecorded (after a snapshot), every statement is IF NOT EXISTS or table_info-guarded, the only observable change was 12 blind-audit triggers the legacy import order would have added on the next boot, rollbackMigration explicitly skips it, and fresh and upgraded databases converge on the same schema (verified: drafts.league_row_id has no physical FK on either path; 011's triggers enforce it). Real defects found: seedIfEmpty is a misnomer that upserts editorial nfl_teams text and the My 2026 Board ranks on every restart, clobbering AI-generated team analyses, user team edits, ESPN head-coach sync and the user's draft board (P1, fantasy-first impact); thirteen route families including the paid-Claude /api/analysis and writers /api/teams and /api/rankings have no auth at mount or router level and are internet-reachable whenever the cloudflared phone tunnel is up (P1 conditional); the daily quick_check took 168 s today on the 11.2 GB database and runs synchronously before the in-process T-60 runner can load (P2); every migration now costs an 11 GB snapshot with a refuse-to-boot disk guard, five migrations from exhausting current headroom (P2). Remaining items are P3 hygiene: 016's mock-draft exemption missed 009's parent-update trigger, a dead role==='admin' clause in modeling/authz.js, code-identity's import regex skipping bare side-effect imports, duplicated root derivation instead of platform/paths.js, a stale FK comment in 006, an orphaned providers.js registry, and a stale modeling/ARCHITECTURE.md. Structure verdict: acceptable — the platform layer is well-reasoned and heavily commented, but the every-boot seed and the tunnel auth gap are live data-integrity and money exposures.

result.label: G04-routes-fantasy
result.summary: This group is the fantasy/NFL-data API surface of Gridiron HQ: 18 Express routers mounted in server/index.js:71-104 covering ESPN player/roster/depth/schedule/news/cap sync, market aggregation (FFC/Sleeper/FantasyCalc), consensus boards and rankings, the draft room (mock CPU brain, ESPN-tab capture ingest, assist/lookahead/verified Claude advice), league CRUD/sync, trade-engine routes, news desk/signals, team pages, local/phone auth, and the dev hub. Wiring is sound: routers also export sync functions that server/services/scheduler.js drives on a timer (espn.js player+news sync, nfldata.js rosters, leagues.js league sync, analysis.js Claude refresh), and every ESPN call in the group is a GET (verified by grep of every fetch, including services/espn-draft.js) — nothing submits picks or anything else to ESPN. Auth is split deliberately-but-not-principled: exactly six families (players, news, leagues, tradelab, trades, dev) sit behind legacyAuthenticated/legacyAdmin, pinned by test/legacy-route-security.test.js; the rest (analysis, accolades, aggregates, rankings, nfl, stats, espn, teams, espn-connect) are anonymous. Fine on the 127.0.0.1 bind, but scripts/tunnel.mjs opens a Cloudflare quick tunnel for phone pairing with no access policy, at which point POST /api/analysis/refresh (32 Haiku calls with force), POST /api/accolades/weakness/:abbr, DELETE /api/espn-connect/cookies and a dozen unauthenticated writes are reachable by anyone with the URL (D1, P1 conditional). Confirmed data-level defects from a read-only SQLite snapshot: GET /api/drafts INNER JOINs league_memberships so all 11 mock drafts (NULL league_row_id) are invisible in the Drafts/Home lists (D3, P2); slot_weakness has 0 rows because the only writer, POST /accolades/weakness/:abbr, is never called from the client, making the 'weakness' unit grade unreachable (D2, P2); espn.js caches the player-identity list at module level with no invalidation, so news entity resolution goes stale after the first ingest on a long-running server (D4, P2); leagues.js GET /:id/data ships raw espn_s2/SWID to the browser on every MyTeam load (D7, P2). Dead-from-UI surface is large: the whole tradelab router, 13 trades.js brain/trend/regression/postmortem/splits routes, all nfldata sync routes plus /sos /roster /grades, stats /projections /teams, accolades everything, several drafts routes (redo/correct/confirm-slot/simulate/GET queue/roster), teams PUT, three dev diagnostics — all still importable/scheduled where they matter, so nothing is orphaned as a module. Overall health: acceptable code quality with good anti-hallucination discipline (evidence-id verdicts, closed-world name checks, propose-verify-retry), let down by an inconsistent auth boundary and a handful of real listing/cache/leak bugs.

result.label: G07-nfl-sim-strategy
result.summary: This group is the NFL play-by-play simulator (drive-sim + policy + learn + calibration), the market-anchored cover/total calibrators and Shin de-vig, the fantasy season simulator and gamescript line ingestion, the T-60 packet contract/runner, and the Wong teaser family (leg rates, scan, season, staking) plus the fitted margin-distribution model. The simulator is play-level Monte Carlo (lognormal/exponential yardage mixtures, EB-shrunk team rates blended with the play corpus, 20 coaching modules, OT, then an exponential tilt of the joint sample to an externally supplied target mean); it is wired only to UI/research surfaces (/sim routes, unified-engine answer card, expert council, live-WP ledger) and no stake or pick reads its cover probability. Its displayed means are tilted to the ensemble's projected margin, so its cover probability is the no-edge ensemble wearing the sim's shape. I found five real mechanics bugs in the engine (turnover field position mirrored, half-clock passed to game-clock policies, inverted kneel rule with timeouts never spent, away-team WP using the home spread sign, a post-OT +7 home-field lump) plus a mis-transformed EP surface and calibration multipliers anchored to hard-coded constants; their combined effect was absorbed by tuning the form-shock sigma to the real margin SD, and the calibration checks are loose enough to pass with them present. Cover probabilities become money only through nfl-cover-calibration's gated logistic offset, and the DB shows forward_gate_passed=0 for both spread and totals, so callers abstain (correct given the settled no-edge finding). The Wong family is the rigorous part: the 74.0586% pooled rate (2124/2868, 1999-2024) reproduces exactly from the DB, the crossing inequality yields exactly the eight lines, ticket probabilities assume independence and the module measures the pair effect honestly; production staking is flat 1u through teaser-season -> nfl-teaser-execution (one paper ticket open). The -115 price floor (set in three modules) admits tickets at roughly +0.4% to +2% EV by the module's own numbers, while the staking module's negative-EV-probability gate that would refuse -115 has no production caller and carries a stale forward SD (0.023 vs 0.0282). margin-distribution.js is mathematically sound (verified design symmetry, conditional-logit gradient/Hessian, sandwich covariance, cover partition, push-at-half-point) and correctly refuses to price the family, but it is orphaned and cites a test file that does not exist. gamescript's ESPN upsert overwrites game_lines.spread with live in-game lines (only closing_spread is guarded), which is the documented source of the 2025-26 research-column corruption the teaser modules exclude by hand. forecast-packet.js is unused by the only packet producer (t60-runner hashes non-canonically) and the capacity ledger has zero rows and zero callers. Structure verdict: messy - strong individual modules, but contract mismatches inside the sim, three duplicated stats toolkits, and several orphaned strategy files.

defects.claim: Turnover field position is mirrored: simulateDrive returns turnovers with the offence's yard line while punts/FG-miss/downs return the opponent's, and simulateGame/simulateRemainder hand the unflipped value to the new offence
defects.snippet: yard = (d.points > 0 || d.kneel) ? 25 : clamp(d.endYard, 1, 99);   // :536; turnover returns endYard: clamp(yard, 1, 99) at :345 while punt returns clamp(100 - Math.min(yard + net, 99), 1, 99) at :393
defects.evidence: nfl-sim-learn.js:439 flips turnovers (`d.turnover ? clamp(100 - d.endYard, 1, 99)`) showing the intended contract; simulateRemainder repeats the bug at :825
defects.impact: An interception at the offence's own 20 gives the opponent the ball 80 yards out instead of 20; short-field scoring after turnovers (a primary NFL margin-variance driver) is suppressed and the form-shock sigma was tuned on top of the bias
defects.fix: Return endYard from the opponent's perspective for turnovers (clamp(100 - yard, 1, 99)) at :345, and remove the flip in nfl-sim-learn.js:439, or flip on the caller side consistently

defects.claim: Policies receive the half clock (counts down from HALF=1800) but every policy and liveWinProbability interpret secondsLeft as game seconds
defects.snippet: const d = simulateDrive(off, { yard, secondsLeft: clock, lead, timeouts: timeouts[possession], ... }, ep);   // clock starts at HALF = 1800 (:460)
defects.evidence: nfl-sim-policy.js:214 `urgency = clamp(1 - secondsLeft / 3600, 0, 1)`, :109 `if (secondsLeft > 420) return null`, :147 `late = secondsLeft < 900`, :243-244 `< 300`, :342 `< 180`; nfl-live.js:62 documents secondsLeft as game seconds
defects.impact: WP override, prevent, hurry-up/milk-clock and the two-point chart fire at the end of the FIRST half as if the game were ending; urgency never drops below 0.5; a Q1 lead is priced as a second-half lead
defects.fix: Pass game seconds (clock + (half === 1 ? HALF : 0)) to policies, or make the policies half-aware

defects.claim: Kneel rule grows the kneelable window with the OPPONENT's timeouts (inverted), applies in the first half, and burns the whole remaining half; timeouts are never decremented so the window is always 160s
defects.snippet:
const kneelable = 40 + timeouts * 40;
  if (lead > 0 && secondsLeft <= kneelable) {   // called with timeouts: oppTimeouts (drive-sim :265); kneel returns seconds: secondsLeft (drive-sim :267)
defects.evidence: nfl-drive-sim.js:461 resets timeouts to 3 each half and :475 `const to = P.timeoutPolicy(...)` is never used, so oppTimeouts is always 3
defects.impact: Any team leading with the ball inside 2:40 of either half ends the half on the spot: no end-of-first-half drives for leaders and no late comebacks against a leader with possession; late-game variance compressed
defects.fix: kneelable should decrease with opponent timeouts (roughly 40 * (3 - oppTimeouts) + ~10), gate on half === 2, and actually spend timeouts via timeoutPolicy

defects.claim: Away-team win-probability calls pass the offence-view lead with the HOME-side spread, so the pregame prior term has the wrong sign whenever the away team has the ball
defects.snippet: const wp = (l, s) => liveWinProbability(l, Math.max(0, s), spread);   // lead is offence-view (drive-sim :467), spread is home ESPN convention (drive-sim :481)
defects.evidence: nfl-live.js:60-75: `@param lead current margin from the home team's view`, `expectedRemaining = (-pregameSpread) * fraction`; same pattern at policy :178 and :213
defects.impact: Away coach's 4th-down/onside/variance decisions are driven by an inverted prior in every game with a meaningful line
defects.fix: Negate spread when possession === 'away' before calling liveWinProbability (or pass lead in home view and flip the result)

defects.claim: Home-field advantage is applied as a post-overtime +7 lump with probability 1.6/7, distorting key-number mass and creating ties/wins after OT has resolved the game
defects.snippet: if (homeFieldPoints > 0 && random() < homeFieldPoints / 7) home += 7;
defects.evidence: nfl-unified-engine.js:44-47 works around it ("a 23% chance of a free touchdown for the nominal home team") by zeroing it at neutral sites; drive-sim header :23-25 claims key-number fidelity is the point of simulating
defects.impact: 22.9% of games get +7 to the home score after OT: OT ties become 7-point home wins, away wins by 7 become ties, and P(|margin| = 3, 7, 10, 14) is convolved with a 7-point spike
defects.fix: Fold home field into the rate blend (e.g. scale ypa/ypc or start-field position) or apply a small continuous nudge before OT, never a post-OT lump

defects.claim: simulateRemainder runs one continuous half with no halftime, hard-coded 3 timeouts, and no overtime, so ties remain ties in live_moneyline
defects.evidence: Callers pass game seconds up to 3600 (nfl-espn-pbp.js:295 `secondsLeft: g.live.clock_seconds`, nfl-live-ledger.js:84); no OT block unlike simulateGame :541-558; nfl-live-ledger persists live_moneyline.tie into nfl_live_possession_predictions (:98)
defects.impact: Live tie probability is far above the real ~0.4% and live WP from a tied late state is understated; the persisted research ledger inherits it
defects.fix: Reuse simulateGame's half/OT structure for the remainder (derive half from secondsLeft > 1800, add the OT block)

defects.claim: The EP surface adds a 40-yard punt to an endYard that simulateDrive already returns from the opponent's perspective for punts, FG misses and turnover-on-downs, so the net-EP table that drives every 4th-down decision is distorted
defects.snippet:
const oppStart = d.points > 0 ? 25
          : d.turnover ? clamp(100 - d.endYard, 1, 99)
            : clamp(100 - (d.endYard + 40), 1, 99);              // punt, net ~40
defects.evidence: nfl-drive-sim.js:393 returns punt endYard as clamp(100 - Math.min(yard + net, 99), 1, 99) (opponent view); for a punt from own yard y the correct opponent start is 60 - y but the code yields y (coincident only at y = 30)
defects.impact: fourthDownByExpectedPoints (:72) and noMansLand (:387) compare go/kick/punt on a mis-shaped net-EP surface; coaching decisions in the sim are systematically off
defects.fix: Use d.endYard directly for non-turnover drives (it is already the opponent's start) and keep the flip only for turnovers once D1 is resolved

defects.claim: Calibration multipliers divide observed league rates by hard-coded RATE_SPEC constants rather than by the baseline the context actually carries, injecting a systematic offset (e.g. ~+8% completions) whenever season/week are supplied
defects.snippet: completion: multiplier(observed.rates.completion, RATE_SPEC.off_completion_pct),   // RATE_SPEC.off_completion_pct = 0.60 (nfl-sim-learn.js:44) while the context default is 0.65 (drive-sim :116) and real NFL ~0.65
defects.evidence: calibrateSimulationContext :110 `completionPct: clamp(context.completionPct * a.completion, 0.42, 0.82)` multiplies a measured-league-mean rate by observed/0.60; the unified engine always passes season+week so this path is live
defects.impact: Every calibrated team's completion, sack, INT, explosive, stuff, red-zone, shotgun and no-huddle rates are shifted by observed/spec ratios unrelated to the team's own baseline
defects.fix: Compute multipliers as observed_before_cutoff / league_mean_used_by_the_profile (from blendedProfiles.league), or skip the multiplier when the profile is already built on the same corpus

open_questions: Is simulateDrive.endYard meant to be opponent-perspective (as punts/downs/FG-miss return) or offence-perspective (as turnovers return)? D1 and D10 are the two halves of that ambiguity and the fix direction depends on the answer.

Does nfl-t60-packet.js intend to adopt sealForecastPacket, or is t60-runner's JSON.stringify hash the accepted packet identity? The frozen SF@LAR observation's packet_hash is not reproducible from the contract module.
Has a pushed DraftKings teaser ever been watched settle? reduced_payout_verified is false everywhere and the grading moves the price gate by 3-6 points.

Is the -115 floor a deliberate operating choice given the module's own empirical pair gate at -116 and 37% posterior mass below break-even, or a placeholder from before teaser-staking existed?

Are the calibrationReport tolerances (+/-3 points on mean total/margin, +/-3.5 on SD) intended to be loose enough that D1-D5 pass, or should the form-shock sigma be re-solved after the mechanics fixes?

result.label: G03-routes-betting
result.summary: This group is the HTTP surface for NFL/MLB betting research plus the fantasy edge toolkit, decision inbox and prediction-engine registry: 11 Express routers, 6000 lines, 371 endpoints, all mounted in server/index.js:96-109 with no mount-level auth. Protection is per-route via requireModelPermission (bearer session + model_permissions) or a router-level middleware (nfl-betting.js:85-99); wong.js, edge.js, decision-inbox.js, props.js and props-tickets.js have no gates at all. Two facts set severity: every locally provisioned session is granted model:* (local-auth.js:72), so the train/execute/promote split is documentation for the owner's own browser; and a cloudflared tunnel is a supported access path (local-auth.js:16-18), under which every ungated route is reachable by an unpaired visitor with curl. Nothing in these files transmits a wager; the only real money-decision path, POST /nfl-market/execution/:id/accept, is gated and backed by exposure-budget, corridor, suspect-price and refreshed-EV gates in the service. Two ungated endpoints spend Anthropic credits (betting-hub.js:878 /explain/page, edge.js:259 /scout/:id) and four ungated POSTs write the ledgers Nick reads (wong tickets, teaser executions/settle, decision-inbox publish). The scheduler, including the T-60 runner, runs in-process (index.js:69, scheduler.js:785) with synchronous node:sqlite, and at least ten open GETs do full-season replays or ensemble refits inline, so a click on the Sim/Research tabs during a Week 1 T-60 window delays the freeze by its wall time. Of 371 endpoints, 176 are called by client code and 195 are not; execution-slate.js has zero client callers, and the betting-to-fantasy bridge (/nfl-betting/fantasy/*) that most serves the fantasy-first priority is unused. Concrete wrong-output defects: nfl-market.js:426 echoes a trials count it never runs, :297 files a posted bet under week 1 while reads default to the live week, and nfl-betting.js:1576/1585 default /who-plays to season 2025. wong.js and model.js are the best-built files (explicit 503s, transactions, sealed holdout, server-side baselines); betting-hub.js and nfl-betting.js have become catch-all routers and are the messiest. Overall: functional and mostly honest about its own limits, but the permission model is inconsistent across files, write endpoints are unevenly protected, and heavy research work sits on the live event loop.

result.label: G06-nfl-council-research
result.summary: This group is the NFL expert council (19 roles, not 16: 12 originals + 5 matchup candidates + 2 external-line roles, plus appended coordinator and combined_decision rows), its v4 coordinator, the specialist/research harnesses, the shared team card, the engine registry/backfill/unified projection, the weekly growth and daily watch jobs, the online neural head and risk lab, and the paid Claude gateway. Every line of all 24 files was read (7,224 lines). The memory claim is confirmed from the live DB: the latest coordinator row (2026 W1 LAR, T-15m) has active_weight_l1 = 0 and shrink = 0 on all 19 roles, so every 2026 combined decision is intercept plus a missingness offset (all values are exactly -0.075 or +0.047). Nothing in the group is on the money/decision path: nfl-auto-picks, nfl-policy, forward-ledger and shadow-ledger never read the council or coordinator; the council even copies the production selection from nfl_pick_decisions and records stake_units 0. Two latent hooks exist: nfl-auto-picks.js:104-108 auto-swaps the projected margin to the online neural head when its self-computed production_eligible flag turns true (currently cold: 0 artifacts under epoch 3, 0 trained), and nfl-model-growth.js refits the live ensemble weekly, which is intended. Only nfl-ai-replay.js calls Claude (Haiku, $1 cap, manual POST; 203 historical calls, about $0.82, last 2026-08-24); no council or specialist file touches claude.js. The most serious finding is that the orthogonal specialist engine is numerically broken: the persisted 2025-W18 artifact has non-finite betas in all six families (serialized as null), final_validation_mse null, and every 2026 forward specialist_team row is a hard 0 that the council counts as a forecast and that masks the legacy fallback. Second, team cards for 2026 W1/W2 were frozen on demand by the council capture 5-11 days before kickoff with cutoff = kickoff but an empty injury table (0 injuries in every W1 card vs 167 rows now), so player_builder and the orthogonal families read stale evidence at T-15m and the growth cycle's weekly backfillTeamCards will hit an unhandled 'team card conflict' for all 32 teams. Historical audit run #32 shows directional rates 0.477-0.526 for every role, consistent with the settled no-edge conclusion. Dead weight: nfl-neural-replay.js (runner has zero callers, audits table empty), nfl-specialists.js (only ridgeFit is consumed), nfl-experiments.js (0 experiments, stale family whitelist that silently drops Roster availability), and the ROI-only ablation in nfl-research.js that nfl-family-contribution.js was written to replace. Overall structure verdict: messy — the shadow ledgers are well designed and immutable, but two reporting paths present non-forecasts as forecasts, the card-freezing trigger is wrong, and several research harnesses are duplicates or unreachable.

result.label: G10a-audit-evidence
result.summary: This group is the audit and evidence machinery: the historical week-chain replay (nfl-blind-audit.js), the one-shot preregistered hypothesis registry (audit-registry.js), the C09-corrected scoreboard (nfl-audit-overview.js), the candidate-findings ledger with its live veto (nfl-candidate-findings.js), the forward and shadow ledgers, the evidence daemon, postgame truth packets, and assorted diagnostics. A blind-audit run is preregistered by hashing the code tree (server/, scripts/, package files) plus 31 input tables scoped by season and a mutation-journal high-water mark; each week opens under a freeze check, computes expert council, postgame truth, three separately-replayed betting markets and player-week replay inside withEphemeralEnsembleArtifacts, re-checks the freeze inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE, and seals a chain hash; runs 27/31/32 are complete at 70 weeks. "Input mutations" are a trigger-fed dirty flag (one row per row-level write on any input table, 5.07M rows, +300-650K/day from the T-60 quote capture, never pruned) used only to decide whether to spend a full rehash. Point-in-time correctness is NOT enforced by the controller: the data hash is season-scoped, so week N of a season is replayed with the whole season present, and the cutoff lives entirely in the callees (nfl-ensemble fitEnsemble beforeWeek + hist filter, weekly-backtest throughWeek=week-1, expert council kickoff cutoff, postgame truth week<? priors). The controller's own reads (Pinnacle open/close archive, nfelo pre-regression, TeamRankings Wednesday snapshot) are pregame-stamped. The candidate-findings ledger never touches replay grading (veto is wired only into nfl-auto-picks), and forward-ledger refuses post-kickoff rows and settles on the frozen close. Defects are counting/labelling, not leakage: scripts return pValue/sampleSize while the registry reads p_value/sample_size, so sealed audits 13-15 have NULL p-values (verified in DB); the overview lower-cases results then hands them to uncertainty() which filters 'Won'/'Lost', so spread_only win_rate_95 is always [0,0]; the shadow ledger settles CLV on the live spread column that forward-ledger explicitly avoids; the findings rule hash folds in nfl-replay.js's whole content hash so any edit stales every finding and the season-end orchestrator throws outside its try/catch. Verdict: acceptable — sound architecture, honest labelling, a handful of P2 number bugs and one brittleness trap; nothing here affects fantasy.

Open week: nfl_blind_audit_runs -> assertFrozen (code hash; rehash data only if journal moved) -> weeklyExpertAudit + buildPostgameTruth + replaySeason x3 markets + replaySeasonWeekly + explainPick/ensembleLine (all inside withEphemeralEnsembleArtifacts) -> weekLookback (nfl_odds_archive, nfl_nfelo_games, nfl_external_ratings, shadow_decisions, previous result_json) -> BEGIN IMMEDIATE; assertFrozen again; INSERT nfl_blind_audit_weeks (chain hash); persistWeeklyExpertAudit -> nfl_weekly_expert_examples; persistPostgameTruth -> nfl_postgame_truth_packets + nfl_game_variance; UPDATE run (final_json = aggregate on last ordinal); INSERT nfl_blind_audit_week_performance; COMMIT
Overview: nfl_blind_audit_weeks.result_json.betting.picks (case-normalised) -> per-market wins/losses/pushes/voids/unknowns reconciled vs by_market summaries -> spread_only + uncertainty() bootstrap

Registry: scripts preregister (name/hypothesis/threshold + services code hash + 6-table row-count signature) -> runAudit(producer) -> Sidak alpha over sealed count, optional mSPRT on result.sequence -> UPDATE audit_registry sealed

Findings: replaySeason(season) -> analyzeErrors weakest/strongest -> recordDiscoveryFlag (nfl_candidate_findings, nfl_candidate_finding_seasons role=discovery) -> recordHoldoutTest via proposeAdjustment (role=holdout) -> promoteFindingToShrink (human) -> promotedFindingVeto read by nfl-auto-picks

Forward capture: game_lines unplayed -> evidence_capture_windows (6 horizons) -> runEvidenceDaemon per due week -> capturePregameSnapshots, snapshotLines (Odds API reserve-gated), SGO, free book feeds, recordNflShadowBoard -> shadow_decisions (frozen once per event|market|model_version), captureForwardExpertWeek -> nfl_expert_forward_predictions

Forward settlement: game_lines.team_score/opp_score + closing_spread/closing_total -> settleForwardPicks -> forward_picks.result/clv_points; game_lines.spread/total -> settleNflShadowDecisions -> shadow_decisions.result/clv_points

Evidence dataset: nfl_quote_batches -> nfl_quote_tape per batch -> chronology quarantine (snapshot_at vs decision, commence_time, book_updated_at as ISO strings) -> contractKey -> rows.jsonl + manifest.json under content hash + latest.json
Provenance check: nfl_expert_forward_predictions.payload_json -> collectTimestamps (*_at keys, ISO) -> compare to evidence_cutoff (kickoff ISO) -> flagged late rows

result.label: G08-nfl-execution
result.summary: This group is the NFL money path: decision board (nfl-auto-picks + nfl-policy) -> append-only decision tape -> exact-contract execution ledger (pipeline/lifecycle) -> human acceptance gated by exposure/corridor/suspect-price/refreshed-EV (nfl-execution-decision) -> settlement from game_lines -> read-only CLV projection against the quote tape; alongside it the book-routing/shopping tools (nfl-execution, nfl-execution-edge, nfl-shopping-board, line-shopping) and the Wong teaser path (nfl-teasers, nfl-teaser-execution, nfl-profitability). stakeFor({source:'model'}) returns zero at server/services/nfl-execution-edge.js:625-633 (`if (source === 'model' && !(provenClv > 0)) return { units: 0, blocked: true }`); no code path sizes a persisted stake on a model probability — every persisted stake is human-entered (acceptance, teaser execution, wong ticket, user bet) or the unset NFL_MODEL_STAKE_UNITS env constant, and the live DB confirms 0 execution opportunities, 0 lifecycle events, 0 decision runs, 0 execution-log rows. Commit 14c5e65 is closed at the line for the four things it names (recommend route auth at routes/execution-slate.js:60, `qualified` carried and enforced at execution-slate-reasoning.js:188/302, assertRealPrice at edge.js:65-74, teaser stake on ev.probabilities.win at nfl-teasers.js:271-273), but three sibling price helpers were left unguarded (nfl-shopping-board.js:32, execution-slate-reasoning.js:108, staking.js:90-91) and nfl-execution.js#rankBooks still ranks a price-0 quote best (a real price-0 row exists in nfl_line_snapshots). The decision tape and lifecycle-event tables are genuinely append-only (UPDATE/DELETE triggers verified live in sqlite_master); the opportunity header row that carries the frozen forecast the gates rely on has no trigger, and the teaser/user-bet ledgers are mutable. The one P1 is teaser settlement grading from client-supplied scores on unauthenticated routes (nfl-teaser-execution.js:307-360), which makes the forward record of the only measured-positive strategy client-writable. Of the fourteen nfl-execution-*.js files, three are orphaned (stress, staking-policy, and clv-downsize which only staking-policy imports), attribution is two-thirds uncalled, and nfl-execution.js's nfl_execution_log is a second routing ledger parallel to the lifecycle ledger; Kelly is implemented twice (staking.js vs edge.js), expectedNetReturn twice under one name, spread grading three times. Structure verdict: messy — the core ledger/tape design is good and honest, but the edges that touch money (auth, mutable side ledgers, duplicate ungated helpers, contaminated-season distributions) are inconsistent. Nothing here advances Nick's fantasy-first priority; picks.js (fantasy draft-pick capital) is the only fantasy file and is fine.

defects.claim: Teaser settlement grades legs from caller-supplied scores with no lookup against game_lines, then UPDATEs a mutable ledger, on routes with no authentication (betting-hub.js:450, wong.js:629; routers mounted without legacyAuthenticated at server/index.js:107-108).
defects.snippet: const scores = Array.isArray(input.scores) ? input.scores : []; ... const teamScore = Number(score?.team_score), opponentScore = Number(score?.opponent_score); ... db.prepare(`UPDATE nfl_teaser_executions SET status=?,settled_at=?,profit_units=? WHERE id=?`)
defects.evidence: nfl-teaser-execution.js:307-323 and :355-360; routes/betting-hub.js:450-457 and routes/wong.js:629-636 carry no requireModelPermission; nfl_teaser_execution_legs stores event_id/team/opponent so the real scores are available in game_lines exactly as settleExecutionOpportunities (pipeline.js:269-281) reads them

result.label: G10b-replay-learning
result.summary: This group is the replay/backtest engines (nfl-replay, nfl-props-replay, backtest, backtest-significance, weekly-backtest, weekly-walkforward), the off-thread report cache, model governance/intelligence/signal-quality/reliability, the fantasy weekly-learning loop, offseason cycle/change, week postmortem, two latency studies, two CLI scripts, and the 1176-line scheduler that drives 52 jobs (26 live on a 90 s tick; 4 metered, 12 growth and 10 heavy all on one 5-minute background tick because server/index.js:67 passes intervalMinutes 5 and .env sets AUTO_HEAVY_SYNC=1). Every betting-side job is shadow/zero-unit; stake authority is gated on model_registry champion state 'production', which only promoteEligibleAudit (POST-only, 0 history rows ever) writes through a gate, while the exported updateRegistry (model-governance.js:170-179) is an ungated bypass vector nobody currently uses. The timer paths that DO mutate live model state are all fantasy: fantasy_coordinator_refit (daily, verified), weekly-learning retrainWeeklyWeights (auto-promotes ensemble weights on its own MAE/rank/coverage gate with no sequential correction or human step), the TD-calibrator persist, and signal-reliability shrink multipliers consumed by nfl-ensemble. Replay/backtest math is careful, well-disclosed and cutoff-safe by delegation; the defects live in the wiring. Three were confirmed against the live DB read-only: (1) the fantasy weekly-learning loop has NEVER captured a snapshot (weekly_prediction_snapshots and weekly_ensemble_fits are empty for all seasons) because Week-1 projections have no `heads` and weekly-learning.js:69 silently skips them, then the scheduler records the job 'ok' 34 times and Week 1 2026 is now permanently blocked; (2) the 'frozen' forward decision ledger is an UPSERT rewritten every 3 h (all 16 week-1 rows share one recorded_at after 66 runs); (3) nfl_offseason_depth_injury is dead after its first run because the scheduler's 'skipped' write (scheduler.js:958) resets the very sync_log row the function uses as its own cadence marker (hours_since_last 6.4 vs due 720). The 120 s job budget cannot cancel work, so nfl_reports shows 'error' for 101 runs while its worker reports (60-83 min each) actually complete, and abandoned async jobs can overlap their own next invocation. Smaller: a tautological red-team determinism check against a memoized function, a proxy prop line that always rounds integers up, a postmortem that grades against preseason params, unused imports, import-time DB writes. Credits: Anthropic is spent hourly on the LIVE tier (nfl_news_signals) and in team_analyses and tweet-line explanations; the Odds API is at 2 credits so multi-book CLV and prop capture are effectively off. Verdict: messy — sound analytics, broken bookkeeping around them.

result.label: G12-news
result.summary: This group ingests NFL news from four writers (ESPN RSS via server/news/ingest.js, twitterapi.io insider sweep via server/news/twitter-ingest.js, the ESPN transactions wire, and the ESPN public API in routes/espn.js which bypasses normalize/store), types it into nfl_news_signals with a rules extractor plus an hourly Haiku 4.5 extractor (nfl-news-signal.js), verifies source identity by allowlisted domain or a live-checked handle (news_source_validation, 108 handles validated 2026-08-29), and exposes the result to a shadow neural head, the expert council's news_reaction candidate, postgame injury carryover, the player-week engine's display context, a shadow fantasy scenario, and one real fantasy action surface (news-lag-trader.js -> GET /trades/:id/news-edge). It also turns verified signals into paid Odds API capture triggers. The 119,639-row nfl_verified_events table is not news verification; it is nfl-event-archive.js's nflverse weekly-roster archive and none of these 16 files touch it. Claude usage is Haiku only, bounded by per-run limits and attempt/content-hash caches (news extraction lifetime ~$0.27; tweet-line explanations ~$0.42); Twitter spend is $1.185 of a DB-enforced $9.50 soft cap. News reaches numerical features but never a production decision and never through the frozen T-60 packet (the word packet appears in none of these files), so Codex return #4 is confirmed undelivered from this side. Two P1s: the rules extractor assigns a story's first-matching status to every player in it, so Lamar Jackson, Derrick Henry, Dak Prescott and Drake Maye currently carry verified released/unavailable=1.0 claims that already triggered paid captures and would drive buy-the-backup actions; and team abbreviations WAS/NO match the English words, misattributing 193 stories. P2s: the largest feed (ESPN API, 1,796 rows) is quarantined for lacking a URL; social verification silently expires 2026-09-28 with no scheduled revalidation; the press-conference keyword filter is a no-op ('ir' matches 'first'); the twitter job is abandoned at its 120s budget every run while continuing to spend; the sweep re-bills the same 20 tweets per handle and reads Schefter as rarely as a second-string beat writer. Overall verdict: messy.

result.label: G10a-audit-evidence
result.summary: This group is the audit and evidence machinery: the historical week-chain replay controller (nfl-blind-audit.js, driven by scripts/nfl-blind-audit.mjs), the seal-once hypothesis registry (audit-registry.js, driven by scripts/audit-*.mjs), the C09-corrected scoreboard (nfl-audit-overview.js), the candidate-findings ledger with human-only promotion and a live veto (nfl-candidate-findings.js), several diagnostics (abstention, slice, passing, candidate robustness, coordination, health report), the two forward ledgers (forward-ledger.js with 0 rows; shadow-ledger.js with 189 NFL rows for 2026 W1-W2), the evidence daemon that is the live T-60 runner, the quote-tape dataset builder, provenance checks, and postgame truth packets. A historical run is opened by preregistering a spec, hashing every file under server/ scripts/ package*.json plus a per-table SHA-256 of 31 input tables, and recording a watermark on nfl_blind_input_mutations (an AUTOINCREMENT journal fed by 3 triggers per table; 5,103,652 rows, +442k in the last 31 hours from the T-60 runner, no pruning anywhere). Each week is then replayed one (season, week) at a time, chained by SHA-256, with the freeze re-checked before compute and again inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE before the immutable insert. The controller enforces no-mutation-during-run, not point-in-time; cutoffs are enforced downstream in nfl-ensemble.js and nfl-expert-council.js, and I found no week N+1 to week N leakage inside these 24 files (the walk-forward pieces in candidate-analysis and passing-diagnostic append outcomes only after the week is judged; carryover reads prior packets and cutoff-gated news). Results are counted from pick-level records with case-normalised outcomes, explicit corrupt-week and missing-week reporting, and summary-vs-picks reconciliation; that logic is correct, but the spread-only bootstrap interval is fed lower-cased results that nfl-replay.uncertainty ignores, so win_rate_95 collapses to [0,0]. Two P1s: both registry scripts return pValue/sampleSize while the registry reads p_value/sample_size, so audits 13/14/15 were permanently sealed with NULL p-values and a verdict forced to FAIL before any evidence was evaluated; and shadow-ledger.js grades CLV against the live game_lines.spread/total while forward-ledger.js (same month) explicitly switched to closing_spread/closing_total because the live column can be clobbered after kickoff, so the ledger the profitability gates count as untouched forward evidence carries an unfrozen close. The blind-audit persist phase rehashes all 31 tables under the writer lock (run 32 avg 21.5 s, max 63 s; run 31 max 414 s) against a 15 s busy_timeout, which will collide with live capture windows. Overall the design is careful and the wiring is coherent; the defects are contract mismatches and a stale close-line source rather than structural holes. Verdict: acceptable.

result.label: G11-props-players
result.summary: This group is the player-prop model (walk-forward replay, TD calibration registry, Monte Carlo board), the prop CLV archive fed by a metered Odds API path and a free Underdog/Action Network path, research-only challenger heads, and four fantasy-side player modules (TD regression, position liquidity, availability, transactions). The replay/audit design is careful (game-clustered bootstraps, Holm correction, chronological calibration), but the production pipeline is non-functional in practice. Root cause: commit 129115e (2026-08-31) made projections.js name every projection by the nflverse abbreviation ("D.Maye"); every prop consumer keys on the normalized sportsbook full name, so nfl-prop-clv.js:98 and nfl-props.js:604/655 have matched zero quotes since. DB evidence: nfl_prop_clv has 101,820 rows but only 406 modeled, all from a single 2026-08-27 capture; the 100,944 Underdog rows are stamped role_ineligible/projection_missing (mislabeled by projectionMatch) and reconcilePropQuoteMatches never revisits them without force, so Week 1 2026 prop CLV evidence is frozen at zero while propEdgeEvidence reports "accumulating". Settlement is independently dead since inception because playerWeeks() names are abbreviated (nfl-prop-clv.js:429 vs 442); 0 real settlements exist. The same abbreviated-name join breaks td-regression.js:regressionForLeague, which the Trends page consumes, so every regression candidate reads as a free agent. The free feed job has been timing out since 2026-09-07 (sequential 16-game Action Network fetch with 25s timeouts vs a 120s budget), so all 14,336 "closing" CLV values are quotes captured 54h-8d before kickoff, 3,386 of them at a different line. The passing-yards estimator bias fix lives outside this group in projections.js:281-299 (opportunity-weighted positional priors, commit f940fa5). The research harnesses (player heads season/weekly, features, prop head validation, SGP correlation) are orphaned or unused (prop_head_audits empty, nfl_sgp_quotes empty). Overall: the audit tooling is good; the money/decision surfaces it feeds are broken by a name-key regression and a settlement design flaw.

result.label: G09-market-data
result.summary: This group is every quote source and every market-data reader: the paid Odds API client, six free book feeds (OddsTrader, Pinnacle, Kambi, Bovada, FanDuel, Rotowire, SBR) into nfl_line_snapshots and the append-only quote tape, the OddsTrader historical archive, Polymarket/Kalshi exchange capture, the ESPN reference-line watcher and capture dispatcher, the T-60 packet/protocol, and the studies that read them (sharp-lag, beat-the-close, line-move-study, CLV ledger, signal latency, live edge). Wiring is via scheduler.js jobs (fast feeds 5 min, slow/extra hourly, Polymarket/Kalshi/line-watch every 3 min) and route imports; captured_at is receipt time everywhere except the archive mirror (book time); book time is kept only from OddsTrader and Kambi. Game identity is NOT unified: the free feeds share nfl:<UTC-date>:AWAY@HOME, the Odds API path uses hex ids, the archive bakes phase into the id, the T-60 runner uses nfl|<Eastern-date>|AWAY@HOME, and Kalshi uses raw exchange codes (JAC vs JAX confirmed in the DB). The T-60 packet is recomputed on demand and only its hash is stored; nothing consumes it; and it can never grant a prospective quote claim because book-feeds passes no receivedAt so all 1,336 tape batches are 'legacy_request_time_only', while the injuries source is mislabelled received_by_cutoff from nflverse's modified_at. Retention is unbounded for every quote table: polymarket_quotes writes 14,000 midpoint rows every 3 minutes (2.3M/day observed, 12.6M total, 0.4% with a book), nfl_line_snapshots ~300K/day, the tape is delete-proof by trigger; no prune exists anywhere. Two files are orphaned (espn-market.js — the one fantasy draft-room market signal — and nfl-bitemporal.js), nfl-live-ledger.js is script-only, and nfl_bet_log/nfl_alt_spread_captures/nfl_feature_revisions are empty. Code quality is generally careful (devig math, clock taxonomy, alt-spread validation all check out); the defects are wiring and labelling, not arithmetic. Overall: messy — sound components joined by inconsistent keys, an unbounded write load, and a prospective-evidence pipeline that is starved by a one-line omission.

result.label: G13a-fantasy-draft-trade
result.summary: This group is the fantasy half Nick prioritises: the live-draft board and its Monte Carlo/verify layers, the ESPN draft capture (chrome extension, bookmarklet ingest, reconciler, REST poller, mock-draft state machine), the trade engine and its sense-check verifier, League Brain, Start/Sit, Waiver Brain, the fantasy coordinator, plus three betting-side files (betting-fantasy bridge, decision-basis, execution-slate reasoning). The career/preseason/offseason player models are routed into all four surfaces (Live Draft via draft-assist.js:1016-1025, Trade Lab via trade-engine.js:425-505/712-726, Start/Sit via lineup-brain.js:114-201, League Brain via league-brain.js:437-438) and are rendered by the client on each page; on Trade Lab, Start/Sit and League Brain they are explanation-only by design, and on the draft board the number that moves comes from projections.js at a 0.2 blend plus the 2021-25 realization table, with preseason-model.js supplying only the p20/p80 variance band to the lookahead. Nothing submits to ESPN: inject.js:75-81 and the bookmarklet wrap WebSocket.send passively and forward unchanged; the only active act is the popup Resync closing ESPN's socket to force an INIT replay (background.js:112-137); the server only GETs ESPN. In-season start/sit today comes from lineup-brain.lineupCall via GET /api/trades/:leagueId/lineup (Lineup.tsx:30), whose week is inferred as 1 from unscored game_lines (NFL_WEEK unset) and whose per-player numbers come from the player-week engine (2025 usage, cutoff 2026-W0) corrected by coordinator fit #12, 2026 wk-1 injuries, DvP and Vegas game script. The most consequential defect is there: week_points is built on adj_ppg (25% current week / 75% rest-of-season) and then multiplied by the full this-week Vegas factor, contradicting the module's own contract that the decision is one Sunday (D01, P2). The capture path carries two real data-integrity findings evidenced in the DB: the extension reported a zero pick baseline during a live draft so 21 picks were attributed to the wrong teams for ~8 minutes until INIT self-healed them (D02), and draft 20 was never finalised (127/128 picks, status active four days later, no scheduler re-poll) (D03). A latent snake-only assumption in board/lookahead/survival contradicts the order_type the mock-draft store honours (D04), and the betting-fantasy bridge compares a local integer id to GSIS ids so its injury/role reasons can never fire (D05). Everything else is hygiene: status-string drift, dead terms, unused imports, a fixed 17-game season delta, a provenance mislabel, a cache fingerprint gap, a nightly identical coordinator refit, and an unmodelled push in the slate simulator. No dangling imports; every consumer route and client page is wired. Overall the group is well built and honestly documented; verdict acceptable, with D01 the single fix worth doing first given the fantasy-first priority.

result.label: G16-client-betting
open_questions: Does /mlb/auto-picks' standing.wins/losses already exclude retrospective rows? MlbAutoPicks.tsx:200 labels it 'Forward record' and the client cannot tell.
Does /betting/wong/season aggregate units_staked / units_won / roi across paper AND placed tickets? That decides whether D-25 is a P2 or a P1 (a dollar figure a user reads as season P&L).
What unit does /betting/wong/board put in candidate.ev_percent? format.ts:54-57 guesses, and the guess is a 100x display risk on the EV figure heading every ticket.
Is GameSimulator.tsx meant to be the /betting/nfl?tool=simulator target (restoring the 'Does it work?' honesty tab), or is the bare FieldSim mount at NflMarketBoard.tsx:197 deliberate?

Is the -115 operating floor (nfl-teaser-execution.js:22, nfl-profitability.js:90) still intended, given the settled finding that the measured +EV is at -110? The UI faithfully reports -115; the question is whether the policy constant is stale.
Should the orphaned betting/GameScript.tsx be folded into Model.tsx's live GameScript (fantasy-priority surface), or deleted? Two implementations against two different endpoints currently exist.
result.summary: This group is the entire client surface of the betting desk: 25 pages under pages/betting, 6 under pages/props, and 19 shared/Wong components — 11,121 lines, all read. Wiring is clean and centralised: App.tsx routes five entry pages (BettingHome, MlbHub, NflAutoPicks, NflWongHub, plus the assistant), NflMarketBoard.tsx lazy-loads fourteen tool pages, MlbHub loads the six MLB/props views, and NflWongHub composes the eight Wong components. Every one of the 128 distinct API paths these files call resolves to a live route in server/routes — there are no dead endpoints in this group. The dominant problem is not plumbing, it is disclosure: the server does careful work qualifying its own output (nfl-shopping-board.js emits qualified:false and unpriceable_reason, nfl-ensemble.js stamps production_eligible:false and calibration_state='research_distribution_only', nfl_auto_picks stores quote_source, execution events carry quote_provenance) and the client declares those fields in its types and renders none of them. That is four surfaces showing shadow-grade numbers with no marker. A second pattern runs alongside it: roughly ten sites hardcode positive tone or a literal '+' independent of value, four sites fall back to a plausible-looking number when a fetch fails (?? 24 heads, ?? 12 specialists), and three sites render an absent payload as healthy because undefined === undefined or !undefined evaluates true. The one P1 is a money-gate integrity defect: both client callers that record a Wong teaser price hardcode reachable:true, and that single flag is the sole discriminator the server uses to decide wong_price_gate_passed — so the go/no-go for the only measured +EV bet on the desk is a free-text book name plus a price field pre-filled at exactly the passing boundary, with no verification anywhere in the chain. The Wong hub is otherwise the best-disciplined surface here (provenance tags, push-exposure tags, confirm-at-the-book banner, a deliberately absent confidence column with the reason stated where the column would be), yet it still carries three number-integrity defects, including a projection panel whose ?? fallback silently renders the optimistic point estimate under the heading 'With rate uncertainty · read this one' — breaking the exact rule its own doc comment says it exists to enforce. TERMINOLOGY.md, which is fed verbatim to the explainer chatbot, has drifted from the code in four places, most sharply on the FieldSim score pill it describes in detail and the Line Shop summary tiles it renames. Two files are fully orphaned: GameSimulator.tsx (zero importers; NflMarketBoard bypasses it to mount FieldSim bare, making the 'Does it work?' honesty tab unreachable) and GameScript.tsx (zero importers, duplicated by a live local component in Model.tsx against a different endpoint, and unable to select the current 2026 season). Overall health: the analytics and the server-side epistemics are strong; the client layer between them and the reader is where the honesty leaks.

result.label: G14-mlb
result.summary: The MLB system models three prop-shaped markets only — NRFI/YRFI (line 0.5), batter total bases (1.5) and starter strikeouts (5.5). There is no moneyline, run line or full-game total anywhere in the tree. All data is first-party and free from statsapi.mlb.com: one schedule+linescore request per season, one gameLog request per player, one boxscore request per final game. Odds come from the shared Odds API pool or ParlayAPI, and both are currently off. The credit-drain guard is real, correct and load-bearing: after MLB odds capture burned 498 of 500 shared monthly credits on 2026-09-01 and starved the NFL capture windows, mlb-pregame.js:41-42 made MLB quotes opt-in behind MLB_ODDS_CAPTURE=1 with a 1-hour TTL, and .env sets neither that nor PARLAY_API_KEY. The system is still fully scheduled and running right now — five JOBS entries, three in the live tier, plus an evidence daemon that plans 106 MLB events per pass and, per due window, loops every game on the slate fetching a live boxscore each. That has written 23,300 mlb_pregame_snapshots and 5,004 evidence manifests since 2026-08-24 into an 11.3 GB synchronous SQLite file, during NFL Week 1 with the T-60 runner live. It has been graded, but the honest sample is tiny: of 138 mlb_first_party_picks, 115 are legacy rows with NULL model_version that standing() quarantines entirely, leaving 23 forward priced picks with a record of 11-12 (NRFI 8-8, K 2-3, TB 1-1). Of 2,635 mlb_pick_decisions only 26 were ever eligible; 2,103 abstained for missing_real_price. mlb_probability_calibrations, mlb_model_experiments and MLB model_gate_audits all have zero rows — three modules have never produced output. No pick has been stored since 2026-09-02 because quotes stopped 2026-09-01, yet mlb_tomorrow_picks has run 104 times since, rebuilding the full 120-player board twice per run to re-derive the same empty answer. The code quality is genuinely high — cutoff discipline is airtight in mlb-projections.js, the Pending-vs-Void rule backed by mlb_boxscore_sync is the best data-integrity thinking in the group, and mlb-shrinkage-fit.js is the best-written file I read. The problem is not the model, it is that nothing has measured it and it cannot be measured before the season ends 2026-09-27. Verdict: freeze — stop the background load, keep every line of code and every row of data, and fix the one P1 first-pitch guard before anything ever re-enables odds capture.
