defects.claim: captureMlbPregame has no per-game first-pitch guard, so 1,271 'pregame' snapshots were captured after the game started and carry lineup_status='confirmed' derived from a post-game boxscore; latestMlbSnapshot then deliberately returns that newest row to the pick pricer.
defects.evidence: The only temporal check is slate-level. The loop at :62-94 snapshots every game on the slate and calls boxscoreLineup(g.game_pk) at :65 — a live /game/{pk}/boxscore fetch — with no comparison of now against g.game_time. The evidence daemon triggers per window but captures per date (evidence-daemon.js:147-149) with horizons including T-15m and close at kickoff-5min (evidence-daemon.js:23-25), so the close window for a 1pm game re-snapshots all 15 games including ones that finished hours earlier. Measured: SELECT COUNT(*), SUM(captured_at > game_time) FROM mlb_pregame_snapshots WHERE game_time IS NOT NULL -> 23300 total, 1271 after first pitch, and all 1,271 carry lineup_status='confirmed' because after first pitch the boxscore has >=18 batting orders, which is exactly the test at :29. validateEvidenceCutoff does not catch it: model-governance.js:126-142 only compares *_at keys against cutoffAt, which is set to new Date() at :88 — against now, not first pitch. latestMlbSnapshot at :127-128 orders by captured_at DESC LIMIT 1, and priceForwardCandidates gates on that row (mlb-auto-picks.js:114-118) before stamping pregame_snapshot_at onto the pick.
defects.impact: No pick is contaminated today only because odds capture has been off since 2026-09-01, so odds_status !== 'captured' rejects everything at :115. I verified all 23 forward picks: every pregame_snapshot_at precedes its game_time. The guard holding the line is an unrelated budget switch. Setting MLB_ODDS_CAPTURE=1 or adding a PARLAY_API_KEY immediately starts writing outcome-era 'pregame' evidence into the forward ledger and into model_evidence_manifests.
defects.fix: Skip games whose game_time has already passed inside the loop at :62 — one condition, e.g. continue when Date.parse(g.game_time) <= Date.now(). Optionally also have latestMlbSnapshot filter to snapshots captured before first pitch.

defects.claim: mlb_pick_decisions abstention reasons are frozen at first touch because the mutable columns sit outside the primary key and the insert is ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, so the 2,635-row decision audit reports first-touch states rather than final ones.
defects.snippet:
run(`INSERT INTO mlb_pick_decisions
      (pick_date,market,selection,game_pk,side,line,model_probability,eligible,abstention_reason,
       recorded_at,model_version,evidence_json)
      VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, date, c.market, ...
defects.evidence: The primary key is (pick_date,market,selection,side,line,model_version) per mlb-model-misc.js:67. eligible, abstention_reason and evidence_json are not in it, so DO NOTHING discards every later, better-informed evaluation of the same candidate. mlb_tomorrow_picks runs every 90 minutes and routes/mlb.js:128 re-runs the path on every page load, so the surviving row is written by the earliest pass. DB: missing_real_price 2,103, lineup_not_confirmed 450, price_edge_below_threshold_or_market_unmatched 60, eligible 26.
defects.impact: The abstention headline rendered by ModelOperations.tsx:144 and the mlbOperations abstentions block (mlb-research.js:70-71) are systematically biased toward early-evaluation reasons. A candidate later priced and made eligible still shows as missing_real_price forever.
defects.fix: Change to ON CONFLICT(pick_date,market,selection,side,line,model_version) DO UPDATE SET eligible=excluded.eligible, abstention_reason=excluded.abstention_reason, evidence_json=excluded.evidence_json, recorded_at=excluded.recorded_at.

defects.claim: modelAudit evaluates a different model from the one that makes live picks: historical slates get no pitcher term (no probable-starter rows exist before 2026-08-04) and no props at all, yet its output is described as a walk-forward audit of the frozen selection policy and feeds every promotion gate.
defects.snippet:
const historical = date < appDate();
  for (const b of historical ? [] : board.batters) {
defects.evidence: Two causes. (1) candidatesFor hard-skips batters at :69-70 and pitchers at :85 whenever date < appDate(); every modelAudit date is historical because :369-371 selects date < throughDate, so by_market.batter_total_bases and by_market.pitcher_strikeouts are permanently {n:0,status:'insufficient'} and overall is NRFI-only. (2) nrfiFor reaches for starters via starterFor at mlb-projections.js:284-287, but mlb_probable_starters holds only 676 rows spanning 2026-08-04 to 2026-09-15; the default audit window is 120 days (routes/mlb.js:76) or 180 (mlb-research.js:33), so for ~9/10 audited slates hp and ap are null and :297-298 fall back to (ap?.run_environment_factor ?? 1).
defects.impact: Every calibration verdict, every gate in mlbOperations, every experiment stage score in mlb-experiments.js:52, and the documented '751 graded picks found an INVERTED calibration slope' claim all describe a pitcher-free NRFI-only model, not the deployed policy. The endpoint's own note at :427 is not accurate.
defects.fix: Either persist a historical probable-starter snapshot (or derive the starter from the box score for past dates as the stale comment already claims) and let historical prop candidates through with a cutoff-safe guard; or relabel the endpoint as an NRFI-only pitcher-free diagnostic and stop feeding it to the promotion gates.

defects.claim: Player-prop grading matches on (player_id, date) with no game_pk and no ORDER BY, so a doubleheader settles against whichever game SQLite happens to return first.
defects.snippet:
const b = rows(`SELECT total_bases FROM mlb_batter_games
                    WHERE player_id = ? AND date = ?`, p.player_id, p.pick_date)[0];
defects.evidence: Same shape at :257-258 for strikeouts, and again at mlb-calibration.js:23 and :26. mlb_batter_games currently holds 2,966 (player_id, date) pairs with more than one row — every doubleheader. mlb_first_party_picks has carried game_pk for prop picks since the forward-tracking rewrite: all 7 forward prop rows have it, the 93 legacy rows are NULL. The comment at :275-277 ('Player props currently do not persist a game id') is stale.
defects.impact: Any doubleheader prop is settled on a coin flip, silently, with a confident detail string ('4 total bases'). No current pick is affected — I verified zero picks land on a duplicated player-day — but the same bug is in the calibration sampler, so it would corrupt any future calibration fit too.
defects.fix: Add a game_pk predicate to both gradePick queries and both samplesFor queries, falling back to a date match only for the legacy NULL-game_pk rows.

defects.claim: market_brier is hard-coded null in the audit scorer, so the market_benchmark promotion gate evaluates to false by construction and MLB promotion is structurally unreachable regardless of model quality — while the UI presents it as a measurable target with a real threshold.
defects.snippet: expected_calibration_error: r3(ece), market_brier: null,
defects.evidence: The consuming gate is mlb-research.js:50-51: passed: metric.market_brier != null && metric.brier < metric.market_brier. metric.market_brier is always null, so passed is always false. mlb-research.js:62 then computes verdict: gates.every(x => x.passed) ? 'promotion_eligible' : 'blocked'. The clv gate at :54 is likewise hard-coded passed: false. GateRow in ModelOperations.tsx:142 renders both with their stated targets.
defects.impact: Two of six gates can never pass for any of the three markets, so the verdict is permanently 'blocked' independent of evidence, and model_registry is written with state 'blocked' on every persist (mlb-research.js:59-61). A reader sees a gate presented as measurable that is in fact unwired.
defects.fix: Either compute market_brier from the stored implied_probability on priced forward picks, or mark the gate explicitly as 'not yet wired' in its label and actual so it cannot be read as a measured failure.

defects.claim: The MLB hub's headline pick counter reads props_auto_picks — the dead proxied table with 5 rows frozen on 2026-07-19 — instead of mlb_first_party_picks, which holds 138 rows.
defects.snippet:
const { data } = useApi<MlbSummary>('/betting/summary');
  const standing = data?.mlb.standing;
defects.evidence: That field comes from server/routes/betting-hub.js:66-70: function mlbStanding() { const picks = rows(`SELECT * FROM props_auto_picks ORDER BY pick_date DESC, rank`); return { tracked_picks: picks.length, days_tracked: new Set(picks.map(p => p.pick_date)).size, ... }. DB: props_auto_picks has 5 rows across 1 date, latest 2026-07-19 — the exact date the upstream proxied pipeline died per mlb-auto-picks.js:4-6. mlb_first_party_picks has 138 rows and is never read by betting-hub.js.
defects.impact: The nav badge at MlbHub.tsx:53 and the NextAction copy at :74 both display 5 picks / 1 day for a first-party ledger of 138 picks. The MLB hub's headline number describes a feed dead for eight weeks.
defects.fix: Point mlbStanding() at mlb_first_party_picks, or have betting-hub reuse standing() from mlb-auto-picks.js which already computes the correct counts.

defects.claim: The 'Odds feed' readiness light shows green 'Connected' whenever an ODDS_API_KEY string exists, even though MLB odds capture is disabled and zero MLB quotes have been captured since 2026-09-01.
defects.snippet: <Readiness label="Odds feed" value={pregameApi.data?.odds_api.has_key ? 'Connected' : 'Unavailable'} ready={!!pregameApi.data?.odds_api.has_key} />
defects.evidence: odds_api.has_key is oddsUsage().has_key (routes/mlb.js:159), i.e. merely 'a key string exists' — true, .env sets ODDS_API_KEY. But MLB capture requires MLB_ODDS_CAPTURE === '1' (mlb-pregame.js:41, unset) or a PARLAY_API_KEY (unset), so captureEnabled is false at :57 and oddsStatus is 'odds_capture_disabled'. DB: last mlb_market_quotes row is 2026-09-01T19:41Z and 2,103 decisions abstained for missing_real_price.
defects.impact: The capture console shows a green odds dot while the one precondition gating every pick is off. The server already returns what is needed — captureMlbPregame returns odds_capture_enabled and parlay_capture_enabled (mlb-pregame.js:97) and /pregame/status returns the parlay reserve (routes/mlb.js:160).
defects.fix: Drive the Readiness light from odds_capture_enabled || parlay_capture_enabled rather than has_key, and surface 'key present but MLB capture disabled' as its own amber state.

defects.claim: ensurePicksFor rebuilds the full 120-player board twice on every call and, when the candidate list is empty, writes nothing — so there is no memo and the work repeats forever. It has produced zero picks on all 104 scheduler runs since 2026-09-02.
defects.evidence: auditCandidateDecisions at :197 itself calls candidatesFor (:180), then :198 calls it again — two full boardFor(date,{limit:120}) builds per invocation, each running ~120 per-player queries against a 249k-row table (mlb-projections.js:374-386). :201 returns [] without inserting, so the next call repeats everything. sync_log: mlb_tomorrow_picks, 104 runs, last_detail {"date":"2026-09-13","picks":0} every time. The same path runs on every GET /api/mlb/auto-picks (routes/mlb.js:128).
defects.impact: node:sqlite has no worker thread, so a slow query blocks the whole HTTP server — the exact failure documented at scheduler.js:1070-1078 as the cause of the app going unresponsive and the reason SCHEDULER_DISABLED was added hours before draft night. This is the MLB tree's largest contribution to that load, for zero output, while the NFL T-60 runner is capturing.
defects.fix: Reuse the candidate list auditCandidateDecisions already computed instead of recomputing at :198, and record a negative memo so an empty slate is not re-derived every 90 minutes and on every page load.

defects.claim: The boardFor comment claims the pitcher list uses the real box-score starter for past dates, but starterFor reads only mlb_probable_starters, which spans 2026-08-04 to 2026-09-15 — so it returns null for every earlier date.
defects.evidence: server/services/mlb.js:142-147: starterFor selects pitcher_id/pitcher_name FROM mlb_probable_starters WHERE team_id = ? AND date = ? and returns null when absent — one table, no box-score fallback. DB: mlb_probable_starters holds 676 rows across 29 distinct dates, 2026-08-04 to 2026-09-15. The docstring at mlb.js:137-141 is honest ('Historical dates without a preserved probable-starter snapshot remain unavailable'); this comment contradicts it.
defects.impact: Anyone reading boardFor believes historical boards and backtests have pitcher information. They do not — the pitchers array is empty and nrfiFor's run-environment adjustment silently degrades to 1.0 for every date before 2026-08-04. This is the mechanism behind G14-MLB-03.
defects.fix: Either implement the box-score fallback the comment promises (mlb_pitcher_games where games_started = 1 for that date and team, safe for past dates), or correct the comment to match the single-table reality.

defects.claim: The pick card labels probability_difference a 'calibrated gap', but it is the raw model-minus-market difference and no calibration has ever been fitted or applied.
defects.snippet: {p.american_price == null ? 'model confidence' : `${p.book} · ${pct(p.probability_difference)} calibrated gap`}
defects.evidence: The stored value is c.model_probability - marketP at mlb-auto-picks.js:133, with no calibration step anywhere in priceForwardCandidates. mlb_probability_calibrations has 0 rows; latestMlbCalibration (mlb-calibration.js:108) is never called from the selection path, only for display; buildMlbCalibration has never run and cannot, since it needs 100 forward priced settled samples and only 23 exist.
defects.impact: The single number a user reads off each pick card claims a statistical property the system does not have. This is the one overclaim on a page that is otherwise scrupulous about labelling retrospective rows and hiding economics.
defects.fix: Rename to 'raw model gap' or 'model vs market', or gate the word 'calibrated' on latestMlbCalibration(market)?.gate_passed being true.

defects.claim: The mlb_logs job issues roughly 1,500 MLB Stats API requests, exceeds its 120-second budget and is abandoned on every run, and is fully superseded by mlb_boxscores.
defects.snippet: mlb_logs: { run: refreshMlbLogs, maxAgeMinutes: 6 * 60, tier: 'heavy', label: 'MLB player game logs' },
defects.evidence: sync_log: job mlb_logs, last_run_at 2026-09-12T06:44:40Z, last_status 'error', last_detail "job 'mlb_logs' exceeded its 120s budget and was abandoned so the rest of the tier could run", 40 runs. refreshMlbLogs (scheduler.js:110-117) calls syncPitcherGameLogs then syncBatterGameLogs for the whole season, each doing seasonPlayers() (mlb.js:151) plus one gameLog request per player. Meanwhile mlb_boxscores has 603 runs all 'ok' and has kept mlb_batter_games current through 2026-09-11.
defects.impact: 120 seconds of the heavy tier is burned and abandoned every six hours, with partial writes left behind from whatever completed before the abort, and a permanent 'error' status that makes the scheduler status page misleading about which jobs are actually broken.
defects.fix: Remove mlb_logs from JOBS. Daily boxscore hydration already covers settlement; season-wide log ingestion belongs in scripts/bootstrap-mlb.mjs, run by hand.

defects.claim: odds_status 'event_not_matched' conflates 'this game was not in the events list' with 'no events were returned at all', making 15,539 of 23,300 snapshot rows uninterpretable.
defects.snippet: let oddsStatus = !hasAnyOddsKey ? 'no_odds_key' : !captureEnabled ? 'odds_capture_disabled' : 'event_not_matched';
defects.evidence: events is [] both when neither provider is enabled and when an enabled provider returns nothing (:58-59). When a key exists and capture is enabled, every game falls through to the default 'event_not_matched' regardless of which case obtained. DB: 15,539 rows carry this status, all dated 2026-09-02 and earlier (the pre-guard era).
defects.impact: Reading mlbPregameCoverage as 'team-name normalisation is broken 66% of the time' would be wrong; it mostly means the provider fetch returned an empty list. A real matching bug would be invisible inside this number.
defects.fix: Add a distinct 'no_events_returned' status when (events ?? []).length === 0, reserving 'event_not_matched' for a non-empty list with no name match.

defects.claim: MlbBoard computes today from a UTC ISO string while the entire server uses appDate(), so evening loads in US Eastern request tomorrow's slate and trip the fallback banner.
defects.snippet: const today = new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10);
defects.evidence: routes/mlb.js:42,62,83,99,103,107,127,154,166 all default to appDate(). After 20:00 ET, new Date().toISOString().slice(0,10) is already the next calendar day, which typically has no stored games, so boardFor falls back (mlb-projections.js:335-343) and MlbBoard renders the amber 'Showing X, not Y' banner at :88-95 on an ordinary evening. MlbAutoPicks.tsx:57-60 already defines the correct localIsoDate() helper; this file does not use it.
defects.impact: A false staleness warning on routine evening use, which trains the operator to ignore a banner that exists to flag genuine sync gaps.
defects.fix: Use the same localIsoDate() helper as MlbAutoPicks.tsx, or have the server supply the default date.

defects.claim: teamFirst's denominator omits the yrfi IS NOT NULL filter that the league prior eleven lines below uses, so a past-dated game with no first-inning result counts as 'did not score' and deflates the team's rate.
defects.snippet:
const g = rows(`SELECT first_inning_home_runs h, first_inning_away_runs a, home_team_id, away_team_id
                    FROM mlb_games
                    WHERE season = ? AND date < ? AND (home_team_id = ? OR away_team_id = ?)`,
      season, throughDate, teamId, teamId);
defects.evidence: scored is computed at :261 as g.filter(x => (x.home_team_id === teamId ? x.h : x.a) > 0).length; for a NULL first-inning value, null > 0 is false in JS, so the game lands in g.length but never in scored. mlb.js:64 writes NULLs for any game not in Final state. The league prior at :269-272 correctly filters AND yrfi IS NOT NULL.
defects.impact: Zero impact today — I verified there are currently no past-dated rows with NULL yrfi in any season, since postponed games get rescheduled and re-dated by the schedule sync. It becomes live the moment a game is postponed and sits un-rescheduled, biasing that team's first-inning rate downward and the NRFI probability upward.
defects.fix: Add AND yrfi IS NOT NULL to the teamFirst query so both the team rate and the league prior share a denominator definition.

defects.claim: candidatesFor builds up to 120 batter and pitcher projections on every historical date and then discards them unread, costing roughly 3,000 wasted per-player queries per modelAudit run.
defects.snippet: const board = boardFor(date, { limit: 120 });
defects.evidence: boardFor runs projectBatter for up to 120 players (mlb-projections.js:374-386), each doing a SELECT * FROM mlb_batter_games WHERE player_id=? AND season=? AND date<? plus a separate team_id lookup at :376, against a 249k-row table inside an 11.3 GB file. Eighteen lines later candidatesFor:70 does `for (const b of historical ? [] : board.batters)` and :85 does the same for pitchers, throwing the whole array away. modelAudit samples ~26 dates per call (:374-378).
defects.impact: Pure waste on the main thread of a process that also runs the NFL T-60 capture, triggered by unauthenticated GETs at routes/mlb.js:71 and :82.
defects.fix: Pass a flag through to boardFor so historical calls skip the batter and pitcher sections entirely, or compute the historical flag before the board build and request limit 0 for those sections.

defects.claim: standing() computes wins/losses/win_rate/by_market over the eligible subset but pushes/voids/pending/quarantined over all picks, so the numbers the UI shows side by side do not share a denominator.
defects.snippet:
pushes: graded.filter(g => g.status === 'Push').length,
    voids: graded.filter(g => g.status === 'Void').length,
    pending: graded.filter(g => g.status === 'Pending').length,
    quarantined: graded.filter(g => !g.evidence_eligible).length,
defects.evidence: graded is every pick (:328); eligible is graded.filter(g => g.evidence_eligible) (:329); settled derives from eligible (:330) and so do wins, losses, win_rate and by_market (:331-332, :346-354). MlbAutoPicks.tsx:200 renders 'Forward record {wins}-{losses}' with detail '{settled} graded · {pending} pending', and :205 renders 'Pushes {pushes} · Voids {voids}' — mixing a 23-row population with a 138-row one.
defects.impact: wins + losses + pushes + voids + pending will not reconcile to any single total, and the pending count (drawn from all 138 picks, including 115 quarantined legacy rows) overstates how much of the forward ledger is still outstanding.
defects.fix: Compute all status counters over the same eligible population, and report the quarantined total separately as it already is.

defects.claim: The Push branch is unreachable for every market because each compares an integer stat against a half-point line.
defects.snippet: if (b.total_bases === p.line) return { status: 'Push', detail: `Exactly ${b.total_bases} TB` };
defects.evidence: p.line is 1.5 for batter_total_bases (set at :79), 5.5 for pitcher_strikeouts (:96, compared at :262), and 0.5 for nrfi (:64). total_bases and strikeouts are INTEGER columns (mlb-model-misc.js:147-166). An integer never equals a half-point, so neither Push branch can execute. The UI nonetheless reserves a status pill (MlbAutoPicks.tsx:49) and a ledger stat (:205) for it.
defects.impact: Dead code plus a permanently-zero UI statistic that implies pushes are being tracked. Harmless today, but it hides the fact that no whole-number line is currently supported.
defects.fix: Remove both branches, or keep them with a comment that they exist only for a future whole-number line.

defects.claim: auditCache is an unbounded module-level Map keyed on a date that rotates daily, so every distinct audit result is retained for the life of the process.
defects.snippet: const auditCache = new Map();
defects.evidence: Keyed at :364 as `${season}|${throughDate}|${lookbackDays}|${cadenceDays}|${fromDate ?? ''}` and written at :429 with no eviction anywhere in the file. throughDate defaults to today at routes/mlb.js:73 and mlb-research.js:31, so the key changes every calendar day, and each value carries a full reliability array per market plus overall.
defects.impact: Slow unbounded growth on the same long-lived process that runs the NFL T-60 capture. Small per entry, but it never shrinks and there is no cap.
defects.fix: Bound it — keep the last N keys, or evict entries whose throughDate is older than today.

defects.claim: Two MLB tables put nullable columns inside their primary keys, which silently defeats ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING for any row with a NULL there.
defects.snippet: PRIMARY KEY (pick_date,market,selection,side,line,model_version)
defects.evidence: mlb_pick_decisions includes side and line in the PK (:67); mlb_market_quotes includes selection, side and line (:100). SQLite allows NULLs in PRIMARY KEY columns of rowid tables and treats each NULL as distinct, so the ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING clauses at mlb-auto-picks.js:172 and mlb-pregame.js:80 stop deduplicating for such rows. Every market the selector currently emits sets a numeric line (0.5, 1.5, 5.5), so no duplicates exist today.
defects.impact: Latent. Any future market with no line — moneyline, or a YRFI-only yes/no — would silently accumulate duplicate decision and quote rows, inflating the abstention counts and the quote coverage numbers.
defects.fix: Declare the tables WITHOUT ROWID, or make the nullable PK columns NOT NULL with a sentinel default (e.g. line REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT -999).

defects.claim: Two of the hub's four views always render proxied components regardless of the first-party source toggle, so the first-party operations, accuracy and calibration endpoints have no ordinary UI path.

{view === 'ledger' && <PropsPicks />}

The first-party /mlb/operations, /mlb/model/accuracy and /mlb/model/calibrations endpoints (routes/mlb.js:82,71,98) are reachable only via the 'Data operations' disclosure inside MlbAutoPicks (:156,170) and the 'Run calibration audit' button at :155.

defects.claim: The reliability-diagram legend names colours that do not match the bars it describes.
defects.snippet: Blue predicted · black observed
defects.evidence: One line above, :275 paints the predicted bar bg-cyan-200 and the observed bar bg-sky-500. Neither is black, and both read as blue, so the legend cannot distinguish them.
defects.impact: The calibration diagram — the one chart whose whole purpose is comparing predicted against observed — is unreadable without inspecting the DOM.

data_flows: Ingestion: statsapi.mlb.com -> mlb.js syncSeasonSchedule (season + first-inning linescore in one request) -> mlb_games (9,145 rows, 2022-2026; 2026 has 2,458 games, 215 unplayed, season ends 2026-09-27).

Ingestion: statsapi.mlb.com -> mlb.js syncProbableStarters(5) -> mlb_probable_starters (676 rows, 2026-08-04 to 2026-09-15 ONLY — nothing historical, which silently removes the pitcher term from every backtest).

Ingestion: statsapi.mlb.com -> mlb.js syncGameBoxscore per final game -> mlb_pitcher_games (101,298) + mlb_batter_games (248,853) + mlb_boxscore_sync receipt (271 hydrated). The receipt is what lets grading distinguish a true Void from un-ingested data.

Model: mlb_games + mlb_*_games -> mlb-shrinkage-fit.js nrfiKs (method-of-moments k) -> mlb-projections.js nrfiFor / projectBatter / projectPitcher -> boardFor. Reads only, writes nothing; every query carries date < throughDate. No look-ahead leakage found.

Selection: boardFor -> candidatesFor (plausible band 0.54-0.78, MIN_IP_PER_START 4.0) -> priceForwardCandidates (requires a captured snapshot, a confirmed lineup, a matched quote, and a >=0.03 raw probability gap) -> diversifiedTop(5) -> mlb_first_party_picks. 138 rows, last written 2026-09-02.

Abstention audit: every rejected candidate -> mlb_pick_decisions with a machine-readable reason. 2,635 rows: missing_real_price 2,103, lineup_not_confirmed 450, price_edge_below_threshold_or_market_unmatched 60, eligible 26 (1%). Frozen at first touch.

Evidence: evidence-daemon (6 horizons per game) -> captureMlbPregame(date) -> live boxscore fetch per game -> mlb_pregame_snapshots (23,300 rows; 1,271 captured after first pitch) + mlb_market_quotes (35,136 rows, last 2026-09-01T19:41Z) + model_evidence_manifests (5,004 MLB rows, 3 per capture).

Grading: mlb_first_party_picks -> gradePick against mlb_games.yrfi / mlb_batter_games.total_bases / mlb_pitcher_games.strikeouts, with canConfirmVoid requiring mlb_boxscore_sync.status='hydrated' before any Void -> allPicks -> standing. Forward priced settled record: 11-12 across 23 picks (NRFI 8-8, K 2-3, TB 1-1). The other 115 picks have NULL model_version and are quarantined entirely.

Dead ends: mlb_probability_calibrations 0 rows, mlb_model_experiments 0 rows, MLB model_gate_audits 0 rows — mlb-calibration.js, mlb-experiments.js and the /operations/audit persist path have never produced a single row.

Credit path: the shared Odds API pool (500/month, 3 credits per MLB game per fetch) burned 498 credits on 2026-09-01 and starved the NFL capture windows; the guard (MLB_ODDS_CAPTURE opt-in + 1h TTL, plus a separate fail-closed ParlayAPI reserve) now holds the MLB odds path closed, which is correct and is also why picks stopped.
open_questions: Does Nick want MLB odds capture ever re-funded? The whole pick pipeline is gated on it and the MLB regular season ends 2026-09-27. If the answer is no for 2026, mlb_tomorrow_picks and the MLB evidence-daemon windows can be switched off today with zero loss of capability.

Which is the intended MLB ledger — mlb_first_party_picks (138 rows, live) or props_auto_picks (5 rows, dead since 2026-07-19)? betting-hub.js reads the latter while every MLB page reads the former, and the fix differs depending on whether the proxied path is meant to survive at all.

Was the '751 graded picks found an INVERTED calibration slope' finding (cited in mlb-projections.js:274-280 and mlb-shrinkage-fit.js:5-10, and the justification for the whole shrinkage rewrite) produced before or after the historical props exclusion at mlb-auto-picks.js:69-70? If after, that 751 was NRFI-only on a pitcher-free model, which changes what the inversion was evidence of.

Is the market_benchmark gate (mlb-research.js:50-51) meant to be unwired, or did the market_brier computation get dropped? The scorer hard-codes it null at mlb-auto-picks.js:418, and implied_probability is already stored on every priced pick, so the input exists.

MLB props are the closest analogue to the one NFL area identified as real-but-under-measured skill. Is there interest in reviving MLB props in March 2027 with a proper CLV linkage (the gate mlb-research.js:54 names and hard-codes false), or is the fantasy-first priority permanent enough that this should be archived rather than frozen?

result.label: G13b-player-models
result.summary: This group is the fantasy player-model core: a structural volume-x-efficiency projection (projections.js), a five-head weekly outcome ensemble (weekly-ensemble.js + weekly-weight-store.js, assembled in player-week-engine.js), a season-long draft-time model (preseason-model.js), an offseason-change multiplier (offseason-model.js + offseason-data.js), and a ring of supporting services (matchups, contingency, correlation, trends, rookies, identity). Every fit in the group is genuinely walk-forward and every decline is recorded rather than hidden - preseason-model.js ships the market curve because nothing beat it, gridiron-model.js reads authority from a sealed audit registry at call time, and role-scenario-lab.js freezes a pre-registered negative result. The wiring is mostly clean: projections.js has 14 importers, scoring.js 16, player-identity.js 23. The headline finding is that the weekly model is correct and blind. buildPlayerWeekEngine re-runs buildProjections({through: season, throughWeek: week-1}) and re-reads priorScores every week, so Week 2 would update automatically - but player_week_usage and nfl_player_week_features stop at 2025 W18 on the live DB, and their syncs (nflverse.js:243, nfl-pbp.js:577) have no scheduler job, only route handlers. So Week 2's projection will be byte-identical to Week 1's, all four outcome heads stay dark (mode 'structural_only_no_current_season_history'), and role-changepoint detection returns nothing. Second, the shrinkage fit and the model have drifted out of unit agreement: shrinkage-fit.js:34 weights evidence by the legacy {1,0.55,0.28,0.12} table while projections.js:109 now applies those k values against RECENCY.seasonDecay=0.35, and the weekly path uses WEEKLY_ROLE_RECENCY seasonDecay=0.05 for the same metrics. Third, an in-season phantom-season bug deflates every player's expected_games by roughly 4% whenever the cutoff season has no team rows. Fourth, the QBR nudge moves the point estimate but never the sampler, so a QB's distribution is centred 1-2 points below his displayed ppg. Of the nine fit-*.mjs scripts, three write to the DB and close the loop; five are offline advisors whose output a human copy-pastes into a const; one (fit-weekly-ensemble.mjs) is never consumed at all and its DB table weekly_ensemble_fits is empty, so production runs frozen 2023 weights. fit-level-uncertainty.mjs's finding was never adopted and the shipped constant is not even in its search grid, while the doc-comment above it is written as if it had been. weekly-ensemble vs consensus-weights vs projections are NOT duplicates - they answer three different questions at three grains, and consensus-weights is deliberate research that explicitly refuses to ship. Real duplication does exist between vegas-fantasy.js and gamescript.js (two independently fitted spread/total-to-volume mappings, different clamps, different consumers) and across five literal PPR scoring tables. Health verdict: the modelling and validation discipline here is unusually good; the defects are wiring, units, unreported components and a stalled ingest - not a model that secretly does not work.

offseason-model.js publishes the uncentred change partial (:1855) while its own comment (:1626-1637) says the centred one removes a double-count. Which convention do lineup-brain.js:46 and trade-engine.js:42 actually want?
Was matchups.js:18 SEASON_WEIGHT meant to be keyed SEASON/SEASON-1/SEASON-2 rather than SEASON-1/SEASON-2/SEASON-3? As written the current season falls to the 0.2 catch-all.
projections.js:157-165 describes LEVEL_UNCERTAINTY as fitted with 'a large floor a and a small evidence term', but :166 ships a=0, b=1.15. Was the fit rejected, or was the edit missed?
Is the ~24-row active shrinkage k vector still the right one now that RECENCY changed? A refit under the current recency would settle P-09.

defects.claim: In-season availability is deflated by a phantom unplayed cutoff season, understating expected_games (and therefore season points) for every player by roughly 4%.
defects.evidence: The weekly path calls buildProjections({through: season, throughWeek: week - 1}) (player-week-engine.js:143-144). When the cutoff season has no rows for that team - Week 1, Week 2, and all of 2026 right now since player_week_usage MAX(season)=2025 - teamGames.get('SF|2026') is undefined, teamG falls back to throughWeek (0 or 1), Math.max(1, ...) makes it 1, and the loop charges one missed game at the full weight seasonWeight(2026,2026)=1.0 while every real season is down-weighted to <=0.35 by RECENCY.seasonDecay.
defects.impact: Every season-points number produced by the in-season path is ~4.4% low, and seasonDistribution inherits it. Weekly ppg is unaffected.
defects.failure_scenario: A WR with 17 games in each of 2023/24/25: availW = 1 + 0.35*17 + 0.1225*17 + 0.042875*17 = 9.761, availPlayed = 8.761, playRate = 0.898 instead of 1.000. After shrinkSafe(playRate, 0.66, 0.574, 0.8) rate is 0.759 vs 0.793, so expected_games is 12.9 instead of 13.5.
defects.fix: Skip the cutoff season in the availability loop when teamGames has no entry for it (or use `teamG ?? 0` so it contributes nothing to availW).

defects.claim: The QBR nudge is added to the point estimate but never to params, so every simulated distribution for a QB is centred below his displayed ppg.
defects.snippet: const meanPpg = structuralPpg + qbrAdjustment;
defects.evidence: params is built at :532-537 before the QBR block (:549-553) and is never adjusted. Every sampler draws from params: sampleWeek :638, sampleWeeks :668, weeklyDistribution :693, seasonDistribution :746, player-week-engine.js:624, ceiling-lineup.js:68. playerWeekDistribution shifts samples by ensemble_shift = ensemblePpg - structural_ppg (player-week-engine.js:620,625), and structural_ppg already includes the QBR term, so the distribution mean lands at exactly ensemble_ppg - qbr_adjustment.
defects.impact: Boom/bust rates, percentiles and start/sit margins for QBs are computed from a distribution that disagrees with the number shown next to them. The calibration gain the file claims (:185-186) was measured with the shift applied to samples in scripts/analyze-qbr-fantasy-signal.mjs:122; production never applies it.
defects.failure_scenario: A QB with a trailing QBR of 70 gets qbrAdjustment = 0.073 * (70 - 53.26) = +1.22. His displayed ppg is 1.22 higher than the mean of the distribution his percentiles are drawn from.
defects.fix: Scale params (or add the shift inside sampleWeeks the way playerWeekDistribution does for ensemble_shift) so the samplers and the point estimate agree.

defects.claim: seasonDistribution silently produces NaN for every total when mult is an object, though the sibling sampleWeeks supports that shape.
defects.snippet: for (let g = 0; g < games; g++) t += sampleWeek(projection.params, scoring, mult * level);
defects.evidence: sampleWeeks handles typeof mult === 'object' explicitly at :674-680; seasonDistribution does not. sampleWeekEvents:604-605 then does typeof NaN === 'number' so mPass = mRush = NaN, randNegBinomial(NaN, ...) returns NaN, and every percentile is NaN with no error thrown.
defects.impact: Latent. No current caller passes an object, but the signature accepts one and the game-script layer produces exactly that shape.
defects.failure_scenario: seasonDistribution(proj, { mult: { pass: 1.1, rush: 0.9 } }) returns { p05: NaN, p25: NaN, ..., mean: NaN } and nothing throws.
defects.fix: Mirror the object handling from sampleWeeks:676-679.

defects.claim: The k vector is fitted under a different recency weighting than the model applies it under, so the effective shrinkage at depth is roughly 2.3x stronger than the fit was calibrated for.
defects.snippet: const SEASON_WEIGHT = (s, through) => ({ 0: 1, 1: 0.55, 2: 0.28 })[through - s] ?? 0.12;
defects.evidence: projections.js:109 ships RECENCY = { seasonDecay: 0.35 } and :116-121 computes Math.pow(0.35, back) = {1, 0.35, 0.1225, 0.0429}. The fit builds every observation weight from {1, 0.55, 0.28, 0.12}. The file's own header (:25-28) claims 'Every dataset builder below mirrors the exact grouping and weighting projections.js already uses at each shrink() call site' - true when Build Order 1.1 shipped, false since 1.3 changed RECENCY.
defects.impact: availability, target_share, carry_share and qb_attempts all shrink on a recency-weighted n. Two seasons back the model supplies 0.1225 units of evidence where the fit assumed 0.28, so the fitted k over-shrinks toward the prior, and the error compounds with history depth - the exact axis Build Order 1.3 was fixing.
defects.failure_scenario: A three-season veteran's target share is shrunk toward the 0.06 positional prior with ~2.3x more weight on the prior at the two-season horizon than the fitted k was estimated under.
defects.fix: Import RECENCY from projections.js into shrinkage-fit.js's SEASON_WEIGHT and re-run scripts/fit-shrinkage-weekly.mjs.

defects.claim: In the weekly path, qb_attempts and carry_share apply a fitted k against a roleW built from WEEKLY_ROLE_RECENCY, an evidence unit an order of magnitude smaller than the fit assumed.
defects.snippet: const qbAttK = pickK(k, 'qb_attempts', 'QB', a.roleW, a.roleW, K.share);
defects.evidence: a.roleW (:404) is accumulated with roleRecency, which player-week-engine.js:145 sets to WEEKLY_ROLE_RECENCY = { seasonDecay: 0.05, weekHalfLife: 5 } (weekly-ensemble.js:8). shrinkage-fit.js:242-243 fits qb_attempts with weight = SEASON_WEIGHT(season, through) whose one-season-back value is 0.55. carry_share has the same mismatch at projections.js:439.
defects.impact: The fitted k for these two metrics is in units the weekly call site does not produce: 0.05 vs 0.55 one season back, plus a 5-week half-life the fit has no counterpart for.
defects.failure_scenario: A QB's attempts-per-game estimate in the weekly engine is shrunk toward tv.pass_att * 0.92 with far less own-evidence weight than the fitted k intended.
defects.fix: Fit a separate k vector under WEEKLY_ROLE_RECENCY for the role metrics, or pass the same recency to both.

defects.claim: scripts/fit-level-uncertainty.mjs's finding was never adopted, the shipped constant is outside the script's own search grid, and the doc-comment above it describes the adopted-but-absent value.
defects.snippet: export const LEVEL_UNCERTAINTY = { a: 0, b: 1.15, lo: 0.30, hi: 0.70, downMult: 1, conc: 3.5 };
defects.evidence: scripts/fit-level-uncertainty.mjs:73-79 searches a in {0.30,0.40,0.50,0.60,0.70}, b in {0,0.3,0.6}, downMult in {1.0,1.3,1.6,2.0}, lo=0.20, hi=1.60. a=0/b=1.15/lo=0.30/hi=0.70/downMult=1 is exactly what the script passes at :104 as 'current (shipped) params' and is not a grid point. Meanwhile projections.js:157-165 reads 'Hence a large floor a and a small evidence term' - the opposite of the constant below it.
defects.impact: Season-total 80% intervals remain at the 0.63-0.70 coverage the comment itself calls the defect, while the comment reads as if it were fixed.
defects.failure_scenario: A caller reads the doc-comment, believes the interval is calibrated, and sizes a trade or a keeper decision off a p20/p80 band that covers 65% rather than 80%.
defects.fix: Either run the script and adopt its output, or rewrite the comment to say the fit was declined and why.

defects.claim: The current season's own games are weighted 0.2 in the DvP fit - the same weight as a game from five years ago - because the season-weight table is keyed one season behind.
defects.snippet: const SEASON_WEIGHT = s => ({ [SEASON - 1]: 1, [SEASON - 2]: 0.6, [SEASON - 3]: 0.35 })[s] ?? 0.2;
defects.evidence: SEASON is 2026 (:13), so the table keys are 2025/2024/2023 and a 2026 game hits the ?? 0.2 catch-all. gamelog() (:37-44) applies no season cutoff, so current-season rows ARE in the pool - they are just discounted to irrelevance.
defects.impact: By mid-season a defense has nine games of current evidence weighted 0.2 each against last year's 1.0. A unit that lost its secondary in August reads as last year's unit all season, and dvpFor feeds ceiling-lineup.js:65, season-sim.js, trade-engine.js and football-context.js.
defects.failure_scenario: In Week 10 2026 a team that has allowed the most WR points in the league all year still shows a near-neutral mult because nine 0.2-weighted games cannot move a number anchored on 17 games at weight 1.0.
defects.fix: Key the table SEASON / SEASON-1 / SEASON-2 (or pass the cutoff season in explicitly).

defects.claim: DvP is fitted over every season with no cutoff, so any historical replay grades a week using a defense rating that includes that week's own outcome.
defects.snippet:
function gamelog() {
  return rows(`SELECT g.player_id, g.season, g.week, g.opponent, g.fantasy_points AS pts,
defects.evidence: No WHERE clause on season or week. dvpFor is consumed by season-sim.js:23 and ceiling-lineup.js:34, and matchupModel() caches the result for the process lifetime (:28,181).
defects.impact: Any backtest or simulation over a completed season is contaminated. It does not affect live weekly use.

defects.claim: A 'Full' practice status overrides a Doubtful designation, turning a 15%-active player into a 96%-active one.
defects.evidence: The guard at :124 excludes only Out/IR/PUP/suspended, not Doubtful. :120 sets a Doubtful player to Math.min(active, 0.15); :127 then does Math.max(0.15, 0.96) = 0.96. The same override replaces the Questionable band [0.45, 0.75] set at :121, which the file justifies at length from the Harvard/ESPN study at :83-102.
defects.impact: weeklyAvailability feeds trade-engine.js:33, season-sim.js:28, role-scenario-engine.js:74 and routes/model.js:18. A Doubtful player is priced as a lock in the lineup solver and the season simulator.
defects.failure_scenario: report_status='Doubtful', practice_status='Full Participation' (a real late-week hedge) yields active_probability 0.996 after the clamp at :129.
defects.fix: Extend the guard at :124 to exclude doubtful, and cap the practice bonus at the status ceiling rather than using Math.max.

defects.claim: The durability denominator counts only seasons the player appeared in, so a player who missed an entire season is modelled as perfectly durable.
defects.snippet: const observed = a.games / (a.seasons * 17);
defects.evidence: :39-42 groups player_week_usage by (player_id, season) so only seasons with rows produce a row; :49 a.seasons++ counts those. projections.js:492-501 gets the same quantity right by iterating firstSeason..through and charging the gap.
defects.impact: Two availability models in the same codebase disagree in the direction that matters most for running backs. handcuffValue (:263) reads this availability as the starter miss rate, so contingent value is understated for exactly the starters most likely to miss time.
defects.failure_scenario: A back with 17 games in 2023, zero games in 2024, and 17 games in 2025 has a.seasons=2, a.games=34, observed = 34/34 = 1.00 and is shrunk toward 0.99 available.
defects.fix: Iterate MIN(season)..through per player and count a missing season as zero games out of 17, matching projections.js.

defects.claim: The published components do not sum to the published multiplier for any player who changed teams - the vacated_share main effect is priced in but never reported.
defects.evidence: partialChangeEffect (:1801-1815) sums every CHANGE_FEATURES term into total, including vacated_share whose COMPONENT_OF is 'vacated' (:1716). But changeSignals (:1747-1763) is an if/else-if: a mover gets only the 'team_change' key, never 'vacated'. So priced lacks 'vacated', components.vacated stays null, and the vacated_share term is nonetheless inside oppMultiplier at :1856.
defects.impact: Contradicts two explicit claims in the same file: :1722-1729 ('not priced into the multiplier, so drivers and the number always agree ... with no small unexplained nudge hiding behind it') and :1796-1799 ('the components are a true decomposition, not an attribution heuristic'). Consumers are lineup-brain.js:46 and trade-engine.js:42.
defects.failure_scenario: A WR moves to a team that vacated 45% of its opportunity and is published with opportunity_multiplier 1.22 and components { team_change: 1.18, vacated: null }. 1.18 != 1.22 and the 4-point difference is unattributable from the output.
defects.fix: Either add 'vacated' to priced for movers, or exclude the vacated_share main-effect term from total when it is not reported.

defects.claim: offseasonAdjustments publishes the uncentred change partial, the variant the module's own comment says double-counts the league-average change.

defects.evidence: :1626-1637 documents that adding a raw change partial to a mean-reversion prior fitted on every player 'charges the league's average change twice' and defines a _centred variant that subtracts mean(train.map(part)). multiplierWalkForward grades both. The shipped path uses the raw one and nothing in the returned object says which convention it is in.
defects.impact: The two fantasy consumers (lineup-brain.js:46, trade-engine.js:42) hold prior-season-rate priors, which is exactly the case the comment describes.
defects.failure_scenario: A stayer on a team with a league-average vacated share gets a multiplier reflecting that average change applied on top of a prior that already contains it.
defects.fix: Publish the centred partial, or add a `centring: 'raw'` field and document what prior it is valid against.

result.label: G17-tests
result.summary: The Gridiron HQ test suite is 175 spec files (31,975 lines, 1,624 test declarations) plus two helpers, one offline guard and sixteen provider fixtures. It is not a smoke suite: it encodes economic claims (teaser leg rates, CLV, Kelly-with-push, Shin de-vig), runs fast-check property tests on the probability/edge/staking maths, drives real migrations against populated fixture databases, and tests cutoff-safety and leakage as first-class concerns. The dominant hermeticity pattern is correct and applied 153 times: mkdtempSync, then GRIDIRON_DB_PATH, then await import of server/db/index.js, with teardown closing the handle and removing the directory. The suite's one systemic hole is the harness, not the tests. package.json:14 runs `node --test test/*.test.js` with no environment at all; the offline guard and the database override live only in .github/workflows/ci.yml:79-82. Twenty-two spec files therefore open the live server/data.sqlite read-write under the documented test command — six directly, sixteen through a service import chain — and since server/db/index.js has no read-only mode, importing it runs PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL, CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, and (in 21 of the 22) a PRAGMA quick_check plus an INSERT into db_health_checks against the same 9.8 GB file the T-60 capture server is writing to. The guard itself wraps only globalThis.fetch, so node:http, node:https and net.connect reach paid providers unobserved. Skip discipline is otherwise excellent: 37 of 39 conditional skips carry an explicit disposition sentence from test/helpers/requires-real-history.js; the exception is nfl-audit-overview.test.js, which silently skips five of seven tests — including the audit path's ground-truth numbers and the run-27-vs-31 reproducibility claim — on a bare boolean. Four files assert on development-database contents; teaser-leg-rates.test.js locks exact counts (2894 legs, 2124 wins, 26 pushes, 74.06%) behind a row-count gate that disarms on data loss and trips on data gain. Coverage: 88 of 299 server service/route modules have zero tests, and the gaps land squarely on Nick's two priorities — nfl-teasers.js (the only structurally +EV bet in the project), nfl-user-bets.js (writes his own money ledger), live-edge.js (the one model that passed its audit), nfl-live-ledger.js, nfl-opening-lines.js (issues UPDATE game_lines and defines the headline CLV metric), nfl-prop-grading.js, nfl-prop-correlation.js and routes/edge.js on the money path; nfl-abstention-audit.js, nfl-specialist-audit.js, decision-basis.js, weekly-walkforward.js and weekly-backtest.js on the audit path. All 16 fixtures have exactly one importer and none is orphaned; several are deliberately adversarial (a pulled BetRivers market, an all-null Hard Rock book, a Melbourne neutral site, the OAK/LV relocation rows), which is a sign of care. Fix the test script first — it is one line and it is the only finding with same-day operational risk during an NFL weekend.

defects.impact: SCHEDULER_DISABLED, NODE_OPTIONS=--import ./test/offline-guard.mjs and GRIDIRON_DB_PATH exist only at .github/workflows/ci.yml:79-82. server/db/index.js has no read-only mode: line 13 opens the file, line 18 sets journal_mode=WAL, lines 22-27 and 171-176 issue CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, and lines 193-196 INSERT into db_health_checks after a PRAGMA quick_check the suite itself records as taking 159 seconds on the 9.8 GB file. 21 of the 22 files do not set GRIDIRON_DB_INTEGRITY_CHECK='off', so each runs that check and that INSERT in its own child process, contending on the live WAL. defects.claim: The offline guard wraps only globalThis.fetch; node:http, node:https and net.connect reach external hosts unobserved, including paid providers.
defects.snippet:
const originalFetch = globalThis.fetch;
globalThis.fetch = function guardedFetch(input, options) {
defects.impact: The guard's own header (lines 5-9) states its purpose is to convert 'no network by construction of the test suite' from an assertion into an enforced property, because a test that 'quietly reached a provider would have passed ... until it cost money.' Any client using node:http/https or a raw socket — including an SDK that changes transport in a minor version — bypasses it entirely and CI still goes green. Secondary fail-open at lines 28-31: an unparseable input is passed straight through to originalFetch with the comment 'there is no host to reach, so nothing to guard.'
defects.fix: Also patch http.request/https.request (and net.Socket.prototype.connect) against the same LOCAL_HOSTS allowlist, and make the URL parse failure throw rather than pass through.

defects.claim: Five of seven tests skip on a bare boolean with no disposition, silently disarming the audit path's ground-truth assertions.
defects.snippet: const run27Exists = () => row(`SELECT status FROM nfl_blind_audit_runs WHERE id=27`)?.status === 'complete';
defects.impact: Used as { skip: !run27Exists() } at lines 22, 36, 48, 58 and 66. A bare boolean produces a skip with no reason. The rest of the suite solved exactly this with realHistoryDisposition() (test/helpers/requires-real-history.js:41-45), whose header quotes the requirement 'failures/skips have explicit disposition.' What goes quiet is weeks_sealed===70, spread_only.bets===153, units approximately -11.855 (lines 25-31), and the claim that runs 27 and 31 are byte-identical across their shared 70-week prefix (lines 68-71). On a rebuilt database the audit path stops being checked with no signal.
defects.fix: Replace the boolean with a disposition string naming run 27, matching the convention every other real-data file already follows.

defects.claim: The teaser regression lock is disarmed by data loss and tripped by data gain — the failure mode is inverted on the only +EV strategy in the project.
defects.impact: Gated at lines 37-40 by realHistoryDisposition(rows, ['game_lines'], ..., { min: 5000 }). If the historical spreads are corrupted or partially deleted below 5,000 rows the test SKIPS rather than fails — the exact scenario the assertion exists to catch. A legitimate backfill changes n from 2894 and produces a hard failure that is not a defect. The file already knows corruption happens: it asserts a 2025/2026 spread-corruption exclusion elsewhere. The policy is stated deliberately at lines 47-49 ('a count that drifts means the population changed, and that must never pass quietly'), but the gate undoes it in the one direction that matters.
defects.fix: Assert n against a stored expected-population fingerprint rather than a literal, and add a separate assertion that the measurement window's row count has not decreased.

defects.claim: When GRIDIRON_DB_PATH is set and the file exists, this test runs migrations and seeds 1,632 fabricated games under real NFL team codes into that database, and never removes them.
defects.snippet:

defects.impact: Line 36 runs runMigrations(), line 40 calls seedLeagueHistory(run), and test.after at line 43 removes only the temp directory it never used. test/helpers/seed-league-history.js:104-111 inserts into game_lines for seasons 2019-2024, weeks 1-17, under real abbreviations (KC, BAL, BUF, SF, LAR, ... lines 43-52) with fabricated spreads, totals and final scores. game_lines' primary key is (season, week, team) (server/db/schema/core-and-fantasy.js:691), so a fully populated database is protected by hasRealHistory (5 seasons / 2,000 games, lines 130-133). A PARTIALLY populated one — a fresh install mid-backfill, or a restored copy — is not: every (season, week, team) slot the real data has not filled, real bye weeks being the obvious ones, receives a fabricated game that then feeds CLV, the teaser measurement and every backtest, permanently and invisibly.
defects.fix: Always use the mkdtemp fixture; never write into an inherited GRIDIRON_DB_PATH. Gate any real-history variant the way test/offseason-model.test.js:627-629 does, and never seed into it.

wiring.problem: none — this is the correct pattern for deliberate real-database work and should be the template for the 22 files that are not gated

data_flows: npm test -> node --test (one child process per spec file, serialised by --test-concurrency=1) -> each file sets GRIDIRON_DB_PATH to an mkdtemp path BEFORE importing server/db/index.js -> DatabaseSync opens the temp file -> runMigrations() or a single migration builds schema -> tests run -> test.after closes the handle and rmSync removes the directory. This is the intended flow and 153 of 175 files follow it.

npm test (local) -> the 22 files in the LIVE DB list -> import server/db/index.js with no override -> DB_PATH falls through to path.join(__dirname,'..','data.sqlite') -> DatabaseSync opens the live 9.8 GB file read-write -> PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL, CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS schema_migrations, CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS db_health_checks, PRAGMA quick_check(1) when due, INSERT INTO db_health_checks. Twenty-one such processes in sequence, contending with the live T-60 capture server on the same WAL.

CI -> GRIDIRON_DB_PATH=${runner.temp}/gridiron-ci-fixture.sqlite -> the first spec file to import db/index.js creates that file -> every later unisolated file shares it -> test/nfl-preseason-blend.test.js sees fs.existsSync true, runs runMigrations() and seeds 1,632 synthetic game_lines rows into the shared fixture. Contained in CI because the runner temp is disposable; the same code path is the hazard on a developer-set GRIDIRON_DB_PATH.

Provider fixture -> test/fixtures/*.json|csv|html read from disk -> the parser under test (book-feeds, book-feeds-extra, nfelo, odds-archive, nfl-external-ratings) -> canonical quote/rating rows -> asserted against hand-computed expectations. No network, no database write. This half of the suite is fully hermetic.

test/offline-guard.mjs (CI only) -> replaces globalThis.fetch -> any non-localhost hostname throws with the host named. Bypassed entirely by node:http/https and net.connect, and by the relative-URL fail-open at lines 28-31. Individual files compensate with mock.module('node-fetch', ...) and per-file globalThis.fetch stubs — the per-file discipline the guard was written to replace.

Real-history gate: 5 spec files -> realHistoryDisposition(rows, tables, requirement, {min}) -> SELECT COUNT(*) per table -> false (run) or a sentence (skip with disposition). The gate reads the SAME live database the tests then assert against, so data loss both disarms the gate and removes the evidence.
open_questions: Is GRIDIRON_DB_PATH ever set in Nick's shell profile? If so, G17-T05's blast radius changes from 'CI fixture' to 'whatever that points at' and G17-T01's shrinks. I did not read the shell profile (out of scope).

server/routes/props-tickets.js and server/routes/decision-inbox.js having no auth (G17-T06) is a production finding surfaced by a test audit. Another reader may own server/routes/; this should be reconciled rather than double-reported.

Is run 27 still `complete` in nfl_blind_audit_runs? If not, five of nfl-audit-overview.test.js's seven tests are already silently off and have been for some time. I did not query the live database to check.

test/teaser-season.test.js:32 claims migration 035 'does not parse'; node --check says it does. Either the comment is stale or 035 was fixed without updating it — worth confirming against git log by whoever owns server/migrations/.

Was the decision to assert exact dev-database counts in teaser-leg-rates.test.js (2894/2124/26) a deliberate regression lock accepted with its false-alarm cost, or an oversight? The file argues for it at lines 47-49, so this is a design question for Nick rather than a defect to fix unilaterally.

result.label: G15-client-fantasy
result.summary: This group is the React shell plus every fantasy-side page and shared component: App.tsx's route table, navigation.ts (the single source for both sidebar and ⌘K palette), api.ts (fetch wrapper with shared in-flight dedupe and a 60s stale cache), state/league.tsx (the one active-league context), index.css (the whole token layer), 28 top-level pages, 23 shared components, four feature modules, and the 489-line ESPN draft-capture script in client/public. I cross-checked every API path these files call against a 527-row inventory of server/routes/*.js joined to its app.use() mount prefix: every endpoint exists — the defects here are wiring, state and presentation, not missing routes. Theme is unambiguously consistent with Nick's light-only preference: index.css has a single :root token block, zero prefers-color-scheme or [data-theme] rules, and the only dark surfaces are the deliberate .surface-deep / bg-slate-950 hero panels, each carrying a comment explaining the choice. Structure is broadly good — PageState/DesignSystem are used almost everywhere, the hub pattern (LeagueHub, DraftHub, FantasyLab) genuinely deduplicated pages, and most numeric formatting is careful. What drags it to messy is a layer of wiring rot on top. The P1 is that the ESPN capture bookmarklet can never be obtained: SourcePill calls /capture-bookmarklet without the ingest_key the server requires, and nothing in the client ever mints one, so the entire WebSocket capture path is unreachable while the tests (which pass the param) and the docs (which describe it) both stay green. Behind it sit a draft-queue seeding bug that can silently drop queued players mid-draft, a capture script that treats an expired key's 401 as permanently fatal and then hot-loops at 20 Hz, a Rules-of-Hooks violation that can crash Data Health on refresh, a DataTable sort that orders negative numbers backwards, and a useApi refetch identity that re-creates dependent intervals every render (killing News's game-day auto-refresh). Navigation has drifted from its own documentation: the sidebar's Intelligence → Matchups entry lands on the Research & Model Lab, ⌘K advertises six redirect-only routes that navigation.ts's docblock explicitly says are excluded, Model.tsx's Availability tab is reachable by no URL and no click, and DraftHub's Recaps tab renders the same component as Mock & boards. Three files (Rankings.tsx, Projections.tsx, PickReasoning.tsx — 494 lines) have zero importers, and two of them hold write paths (ranking reorder/tier/note, consensus-board creation) that exist nowhere else in the client, so they are lost capability rather than plain dead code.

defects.claim: The ESPN draft-capture bookmarklet can never be obtained from the UI: SourcePill requests /drafts/:id/capture-bookmarklet without the ingest_key the server requires, and no client code ever mints one — so the entire WebSocket capture path is unreachable.
defects.snippet: const out = await api<{ href?: string }>(`/drafts/${draftId}/capture-bookmarklet`);
defects.evidence: server/routes/draft-capture.js:41-43 resolveIngestKey() reads only req.query.ingest_key; :59-62 returns 400 {error:'ingest_key required: pass ?ingest_key=… obtained from POST /api/drafts/:id/ingest-key'} when absent. grep -rn 'ingest-key|ingest_key' client/src client/public yields exactly one hit — draft-capture.js:156, inside the payload itself — so nothing in the client ever calls POST /drafts/:id/ingest-key. test/draft-capture-route.test.js:58-80 exercises the route WITH ?ingest_key=k1, and docs/reference/fantasy/DRAFT_CAPTURE.md:17 documents the UI as calling it with the param, so neither tests nor docs catch the gap.
defects.impact: Clicking 'Get the ESPN tab bookmarklet' on Live Draft always renders SourcePill.tsx:73 'Bookmarklet unavailable — ingest_key required: …'. The 489-line client/public/draft-capture.js, server/services/draft-ingest.js, POST /drafts/:id/capture, GET /drafts/:id/ingest-status and SourcePill's 'Fed by your ESPN tab' state are all dead in practice. Nick's recorded draft-night setup is 'laptop + ESPN + one bookmarklet'; that flow cannot be started. Live Draft still works via the 4s server-side poll (LiveDraft.tsx:202), so the board is not blind — but the low-latency capture the UI advertises cannot be turned on.
defects.fix: Have SourcePill first POST /drafts/:id/ingest-key and pass the key as ?ingest_key=… (the route's comment at draft-capture.js:33-38 explains why it deliberately refuses to mint, so the client is the right place).

defects.claim: The draft queue only latches its seeded flag when the server queue is non-empty, so a mid-draft poll can silently overwrite optimistic local queue edits.
defects.snippet: if (!seeded.current && serverQueue.length) { setQueue(serverQueue); seeded.current = true; }
defects.evidence: A draft begins with an empty queue, so serverQueue.length is 0 and seeded.current stays false. The call site DraftRoom.tsx:59 — useDraftQueue(id, draft?.my_slot ?? 1, draft?.queue.map(q => q.player_id) ?? []) — builds a new array identity every render, so the [serverQueue] effect re-evaluates continuously until it finally latches.
defects.impact: Queue three players quickly (local [a,b,c], three PUTs in flight), then a refetch triggered by a CPU pick returns a snapshot taken after only the first PUT landed (serverQueue=[a]). The effect fires — still unseeded, length>0 — and setQueue([a]) drops b and c from the UI even though the server holds them, with no error and no indication. On draft night the queue is what you read while the clock runs.
defects.fix: Latch seeded on the first render where serverQueue is defined at all, or reconcile by merging server and local ids rather than replacing.

defects.claim: The capture script treats every 4xx — including the 401 an expired ingest key produces — as permanently fatal, cannot be recovered by re-clicking the bookmarklet, and then spins its scheduler at 20 Hz for the rest of the draft.
defects.snippet:
if (status >= 400 && status < 500 && status !== 429) {
          state.fatal = true;
defects.evidence: server/routes/drafts.js:268-270 returns 401 for a key that is wrong OR expired ('ingest key is wrong or expired — mint a new one in the draft room'); keys expire at draft_at+8h or a default window (server/services/draft-ingest.js:36-48). Once fatal, flush() short-circuits at :188 forever. fatal does not set stopped, so the boot guard at :475-479 (…state && !state.stopped) reports 'already running … not attaching twice' and only un-dismisses the pill. At :268 the scheduler delay is `state.outbox.length && !state.inflight && now() >= state.blockedUntil ? 50 : BATCH_MS`; after a fatal one heartbeat batch sits in the outbox with inflight=false and blockedUntil=0, so schedule() re-fires every 50 ms while flush() returns immediately.
defects.impact: A draft running past the key window silently loses its frame feed mid-draft, the pill reads 'STOPPED', and the only documented recovery — re-clicking the bookmarklet — is refused by the guard, leaving reloading the ESPN tab as the sole option, which SourcePill.tsx:70 explicitly tells the user never to do. Meanwhile the ESPN tab burns CPU at 20 Hz for the rest of the draft.
defects.fix: Treat 401/429/5xx as retryable with backoff and reserve fatal for 403/404; have the fatal path either stop the scheduler or clear the re-attach guard.

defects.claim: Rules-of-Hooks violation: SourceTable returns before calling useMemo, so a source list that goes from empty to non-empty across a refetch throws 'Rendered more hooks than during the previous render' and takes down the Data Health page.
defects.snippet:
if (sources.length === 0) return null;
  const sorted = useMemo(() => [...sources].sort(stalestFirst), [sources]);
defects.evidence: SourceTable is rendered twice, at DataHealth.tsx:404 with `scheduled` and :405 with `manual`. The early return at :156 sits above the useMemo at :157, so a render with an empty list executes 0 hooks and a render with a non-empty list executes 1.
defects.impact: Press '↻ Refresh everything' (:300 → runRefreshAll → refetch() at :274). If the new /dev/sources payload contains a manual or scheduled source the previous payload lacked, React throws on the hook-count change; the page unmounts to an error boundary or blank screen and the refresh result the user was waiting for is lost.
defects.fix: Move the `if (sources.length === 0) return null;` guard below the useMemo — the memo is not load-bearing for a ~30-row sort anyway.

defects.claim: DataTable sorts every column with localeCompare({numeric:true}), which ignores the minus sign — negative numbers sort in reverse magnitude order and ahead of zero.
defects.snippet: if (sort) { const col = columns.find(c => c.key === sort.key); if (col?.sortValue) out = [...out].sort((a, b) => String(col.sortValue!(a) ?? '').localeCompare(String(col.sortValue!(b) ?? ''), undefined, { numeric: true }) * sort.dir); }
defects.evidence: Verified in node with ['-2.28','-10.5','3','-1.5','12','0']: numeric localeCompare yields ['-1.5','-2.28','-10.5','0','3','12'] while true numeric ordering is ['-10.5','-2.28','-1.5','0','3','12']. ICU numeric collation treats '-' as a separator, not a sign. Separately a null sortValue becomes the string 'null' and sorts among text.
defects.impact: Any DataTable column that can go negative — CLV, edge, point differential, market-value delta, projection bias — is silently mis-ranked when sorted, and it looks plausible because magnitudes are ordered. A user sorting 'worst CLV first' gets -1.5 above -10.5.
defects.fix: Branch on typeof sortValue: subtract for numbers, localeCompare only for strings, sort nulls to a fixed end.

defects.claim: useApi returns a brand-new refetch closure every render, so any effect that lists refetch in its dependency array re-runs on every render — which kills News's game-day 60-second auto-refresh.
defects.snippet: return { data, loading, refreshing, error, refetch: () => refetch(true) };
defects.evidence: The inner refetch is a useCallback (api.ts:111-160) but the returned wrapper is a fresh arrow literal each render. Concrete victim, News.tsx:56-60: useEffect(() => { if (!data?.signals?.some(s => s.tracking?.status === 'game_day')) return; const timer = window.setInterval(() => refetch(), 60_000); return () => window.clearInterval(timer); }, [data?.signals, refetch]);
defects.impact: Every render tears down and recreates the 60s interval. On a page that re-renders more often than once a minute — typing in the team select at News.tsx:73, a sibling useApi resolving, any parent re-render — the interval is cleared before it ever fires, so the live game-day model check never refreshes. That is exactly the NFL-Sunday behaviour the effect exists to provide.
defects.fix: Wrap the returned refetch in useCallback keyed on the inner refetch, or expose it through a ref so its identity is stable.

So the server can derive the current week; only ceiling-lineup pins it. CeilingLineup's own render (MyTeam.tsx:345-451) never prints a week.

return state.available.find((a: any) => a.name === advice.pick)

defects.claim: consistencyText mixes its numerator and denominator from two different payload shapes, so a player carrying both forms can render an impossible ratio.
defects.snippet:
const c = ev.career?.consistency ?? ev.consistency;
  const n = ev.consistency?.seasons_counted ?? ev.career?.seasons?.length ?? null;
defects.evidence: c prefers the full form (ev.career.consistency) while n prefers the compact form (ev.consistency.seasons_counted) — opposite precedence. The function's own docstring says 'from whichever form of the consistency counts is present', i.e. either/or was the intent.

defects.fix: Pick one form first and read both the count and the denominator from it.

defects.claim: The ceiling-vs-mean comparison hard-codes a '+' prefix on a value that can be negative, rendering '+-0.40pp more likely to clear the target'.

Line 437 does the same for +{v.ceiling_gained}.

defects.claim: Batch size is checked against the JSON-serialized frame length while the per-frame cap is applied before serialization, so a quote-dense frame can produce an over-budget batch that is sent anyway.
defects.snippet: if (frames.length && (size + fsize > MAX_BODY_BYTES || frames.length >= MAX_FRAMES_PER_BATCH)) break;
defects.evidence: enqueueFrame truncates at MAX_FRAME_BYTES (44 KB) on the raw text (:141-145), but buildBatches measures byteLength(JSON.stringify(f)) (:173), which inflates every quote to \" and every non-ASCII char to \uXXXX. The `frames.length &&` guard means the first frame of a batch is pushed regardless of size, so a frame that serializes past MAX_BODY_BYTES (48 KB) forms an oversize batch on its own.
defects.impact: The server rejects the oversize body with a 4xx, which G15-D03's fatal handler then treats as permanent — turning a single malformed frame into the end of capture for the whole draft.
defects.fix: Measure the per-frame cap on the serialized form, or split an over-budget single frame rather than sending it.

data_flows: Auth: api() reads localStorage['gridiron_session_token'] → Authorization: Bearer. A 401 triggers a one-shot POST /api/auth/local-session (api.ts:16-31); a 403 with {pairing:true} redirects to /pair?next=… where Pair.tsx POSTs /api/auth/pair with an 8-digit code and stores the returned token.

Read caching: every useApi GET goes through sharedGet(), which joins an identical in-flight request and serves a <60s cached response; refetch(true) always bypasses. This is what keeps repeated /edge/vor, /rankings and /leagues reads across pages to one network call.
Active league: GET /leagues → LeagueProvider → localStorage['gh:activeLeague'] → consumed by Home, MyTeam, Leagues, Lineup, LeagueBrain, Trends, TradeLab and Model to build every league-scoped path.

Fantasy roster chain: /leagues/:id/data (raw platform payload) and /trades/:id/rosters (modelled assets) → MyTeam and TradeLab; /trades/:id/scout drives both MyTeam's header stats and TeamScout, fetched once by the parent and passed down as a prop.

Start/sit chain: /trades/:id/lineup (server derives the week) → Lineup.tsx slots, each carrying evidence rendered by EvidenceStrip → EvidenceTable/StreakChips. /trades/:id/ceiling-lineup is the parallel ceiling path and is the one that pins week=1.

Draft chain (mock): GET /drafts/:id → DraftRoom board + available; POST /picks, /cpu-pick, /pause, /sim-to-end; DELETE /picks/last; PUT /queue via useDraftQueue; GET /recommendation drives the on-the-clock banner and the 0:00 auto-pick.

Draft chain (live): POST /drafts/live/link creates the mirror → POST /drafts/:id/sync every 4s pulls ESPN server-side → GET /assist repaints the board → GET /advice and /lookahead fire when picks-until-my-turn <= 3. The optional low-latency path (browser bookmarklet → POST /drafts/:id/capture → GET /ingest-status → SourcePill) is currently unreachable.

Player identity: headshotUrl() prefers espn_id (a.espncdn.com) then sleeper_id (sleepercdn.com), returning null so Headshot/Face can fall back to initials — ESPN serves a transparent PNG rather than a 404, which LiveDraft's Face component handles explicitly.

Per-viewer local state: localStorage holds gh:sidebar, gh:activeLeague, gh:recent-routes, gh:untouchable:<leagueId>, gh:trades-seen:<league>:<team>, gh:trades-batch-seen:<league>:<team>; sessionStorage holds espn-gate-dismissed and data-setup-dismissed (deliberately per-sitting so a missing-data install keeps being reminded). Every read is try/catch wrapped.

Betting reads from this group: NflMarketBoard calls /betting/status, /nfl-betting/ai-replay/latest, /nfl-market/picks/candidates, /nfl-market/bets, /nfl-market/sync-and-pick, /nfl-betting/lines/sync-now and /nfl-betting/explain/ai; DataHealth calls /betting/summary and /nfl-market/prospective-collection/run. All exist server-side.
open_questions: Were Rankings.tsx and Projections.tsx meant to be folded into Players.tsx or parked? Their write paths — PUT /rankings/:id/entries (reorder/tier/note) and POST /aggregates/create-board — have no other client call site, so deleting them removes capability while keeping them leaves dead files that ⌘K still advertises.

Should /matchups point at TradeLab's Matchups tab (TradeLab.tsx:1081) rather than FantasyLab? That would make the sidebar label honest with a one-line route change and leave /lab as the only entry to the model lab.

G15-D01 blocks the documented draft-night bookmarklet flow. Is the intended fix client-side (SourcePill mints via POST /drafts/:id/ingest-key first), or has the WebSocket capture been quietly retired in favour of the 4s server-side poll? The docs and tests still describe it as live.
Should Model.tsx's Availability tab be added to FantasyLab's engine tab list, or was it intentionally retired? The endpoint (/model/availability) is live and the component is complete.

NflMarketBoard and MyTeam's CeilingLineup both hard-code a week. Is there a canonical 'current NFL week' the client should read (the candidates payload carries season/week), or should each surface keep deriving its own?

result.label: G13c-infra-misc
result.summary: This group is the infrastructure spine: nine shared services (stats, formatting, dates, caching, confidence tiers, football context, the football-first residual model, the connectivity auditor, live scoreboard) plus the entire install/launch/tunnel/packaging/CI path. Engineering quality is genuinely high — SHA-256 verification of the Node tarball in both installers, CI Actions pinned to commit hashes, a real enforced offline guard on the test step, isolated temp databases for the smoke test; and stats-util's Holm-Bonferroni, Acklam probit, Cholesky-with-jitter and Marsaglia-Tsang samplers are all correct on line-by-line verification. Note the focus question's premise is wrong: there is no SE helper and no bootstrap in stats-util — those live in backtest-significance.js and the bootstrap tests, which build on these primitives. The dominant defect shape is not sloppy code but a correct, well-argued docstring paired with an implementation that does not deliver it. import-scottfree.mjs declares an OUTCOME_COLUMNS leakage guard and never references it, so home_total_points/away_total_points — this game's own score — fall into features_json unmarked (P1, verified by diffing the two lists). package-release.mjs promises the database is excluded and its non-git fallback would sweep the 11.3 GB live data.sqlite into the release zip (P1). system-connectivity.js promises to find dead code but scans only 3 of server/'s 11 code directories and reports healthy:true when it cannot read the tree at all, so it can name a live module used by the T-60 runner as deletable (P2). football-first.js promises to abstain when every feature is zero, but the later carryover feature makes weeks 1-4 non-zero, so it emits leans this weekend from a distribution it never trained on — it trains only on week>=5 (P2). nfl-live.js promises never to assert 0%/100% on a live game and returns exactly 1.0 in overtime (P2). compute-cache.js documents that cached() must never be called from a route, and nfl-betting.js:1752 does exactly that with a ~90 s fit whose fingerprint busts on any single row insert into game_lines — live during Week 1 capture (P1). Separately I confirmed against ps that the live server PID 56651 was started by launcher.mjs:75 detached and is NOT node --watch, and that scripts/tunnel.mjs (PID 50971) is dead while its cloudflared child (50981) is orphaned and still publicly serving :5177 — the launcher probes the child, so it reports "already running" forever and can never restart the registrar, leaving phone access broken and an unmanaged public ingress the app no longer knows about (P1). The 16-line lint is node --check only — pure parseability, zero semantic analysis — which is the enabling condition for most of the P3s including the dead OUTCOME_COLUMNS. Verdict: the shared math is trustworthy; the operational and packaging guarantees are not yet what their comments claim.
