defects.claim: The OUTCOME_COLUMNS leakage guard is declared and never referenced, so two of this game's own outcome columns are written into features_json as if they were pregame features.
defects.evidence: grep shows OUTCOME_COLUMNS appears exactly twice: once in a comment at L10 and once at its own declaration at L42. It is never read. Diffing the two lists programmatically, the outcome columns present in OUTCOME_COLUMNS but absent from TOP_LEVEL are exactly ['home_total_points','away_total_points'] — so those two fall through the L113 continue and land in featureRow.
defects.impact: This game's own final scores sit inside features_json alongside genuine pregame features, unmarked and indistinguishable by key. Any consumer that treats the keys of features_json as its feature set trains on the label, producing a perfect in-sample fit that collapses out of sample. The script's own closing reminder at L135-137 names '*_total_points' as outcome data that must never be fed to a pregame model — the warning is printed, the code does not enforce it.
defects.fix: Change L113 to `if (TOP_LEVEL.includes(k) || OUTCOME_COLUMNS.has(k)) continue;`, or nest outcomes under an explicit features_json.outcome sub-object so a key-enumerating consumer cannot sweep them in.

defects.claim: startTunnel() probes for the cloudflared CHILD rather than the tunnel.mjs registrar that owns URL registration, so an orphaned cloudflared makes the launcher report 'already running' forever and never restart the dead registrar.
defects.snippet: if (processRunning(`cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:${APP_PORT}`)) return 'already running';
defects.evidence: ps -axo pid,ppid,command shows cloudflared PID 50981 with ppid 50971, and NO process 50971 exists — scripts/tunnel.mjs is dead and its child is orphaned and still serving. server/data/launcher-logs/tunnel.log last changed 01:36 (a live 30 s re-register interval would keep it current) and its tail is hundreds of consecutive 'could not register the tunnel with the app: fetch failed' lines. I executed the predicate directly: it returns true for this pattern and false for a control pattern, confirming a genuine match on the orphan.
defects.impact: Two consequences. (1) Availability: tunnel.mjs:62-64 is the ONLY thing that re-registers the URL with the app every 30 s, so /api/auth/tunnel-url stays null and phone access cannot be restored without manual intervention — on NFL Week 1 weekend. (2) Exposure: a public trycloudflare.com hostname is still tunnelling to :5177 with no process managing it, and because registration failed, nothing in the app's UI indicates the app is publicly reachable. The comment at L82-88 records a previous fix for this same symptom ('Found 2026-09-07 chasing why /api/auth/tunnel-url stayed null despite /start reporting success') which narrowed the pattern and addressed a different cause, leaving this one untouched.
defects.fix: Check liveness of the registrar, not the child: pgrep for scripts/tunnel.mjs, or call GET /api/auth/tunnel-url (which this file already knows how to do at L58-70) and respawn when it returns null. Then kill orphaned cloudflared PID 50981 and restart tunnel.mjs.

defects.claim: A GET route runs the ~90-second football-first ridge fit synchronously on the Express request thread, against an explicit prohibition written in compute-cache.js itself.
defects.evidence: footballFirstLean (football-first.js:361) calls residualModel, which at football-first.js:345 calls cached(), which computes on a miss. compute-cache.js:60-64 states: 'cached() computes on a miss, which is right for a background job and wrong inside a route — a ninety-second fit called from an Express handler blocks the whole event loop and takes every other endpoint down with it.' peekResidualModel exists for exactly this (football-first.js:339), is imported at nfl-betting.js:5, and IS used at nfl-betting.js:1782 — just not in this handler. The sibling POST /football-first/fit at L1799-1810 goes out of band to a worker with the note 'Fitting in a worker thread (~90 s)'.
defects.impact: The cache fingerprint at football-first.js:346-348 includes COUNT(*) on game_lines, nfl_injuries and nfl_team_week_features, so ANY single inserted row busts it. It is NFL Week 1 and a T-60 capture runner is writing game_lines live. One GET to this endpoint after any capture blocks the event loop for ~90 s, stalling the capture runner that shares it. Additionally report-cache.js:56 pre-warms residualModel in a WORKER THREAD, which has its own module instance and therefore its own store Map, so the pre-warm cannot populate the main thread's cache at all.
defects.fix: Use peekResidualModel in the GET handler and return 202 with a queued-fit pointer on a miss, exactly as POST /football-first/fit already does.

defects.claim: The non-git fallback path in the release packager would sweep the 11.3 GB live database into the distributable zip, contradicting the module's own header guarantee.
defects.evidence: L167-174 falls back to walk(ROOT) when `git ls-files` throws. walk() filters only on exact basename against EXCLUDE. The entry 'data' matches the directory server/data, but the database file is server/data.sqlite — ls -la confirms server/data.sqlite at 11,302,981,632 bytes, server/data.sqlite-wal at 3,346,807,872 bytes, and server/data.sqlite.pre-migration-....bak at 9,788,506,112 bytes. None of those basenames are in EXCLUDE. The git path is safe only because git ls-files respects .gitignore, which L165-166 states explicitly.
defects.impact: In any non-git checkout (an extracted release, a tarball copy, a checkout with a broken .git) the release zip would carry the live database, which per .gitignore:4 'contains ESPN league cookies and your personal rankings/drafts'. The header at L25-27 promises the opposite in as many words: 'node_modules, .env, the database and .git are excluded ... the database holds league data — shipping either would be handing them to whoever gets the file.'
defects.fix: Add a /^data\.sqlite/ pattern test to walk()'s exclusion, or make the fallback refuse to run and require a git checkout.

defects.claim: The model trains only on week>=5 but scores any week, and in weeks 1-4 the carryover path substitutes last-season values — so the same feature names carry a different meaning at serve time, and the abstention guard that was the safety net no longer fires.
defects.evidence: I traced Week 1 2026 through every feature. availability_edge = 0 (availabilityPicture reads week < 1, no rows) and qb_downgrade_edge = 0 (same), but efficiency_edge, pace_edge and script_conflict are all NON-zero via the 2025 carryover at L185-196. The abstain guard at L377 is `FEATURES.filter(spec => Math.abs(f[spec.key] ?? 0) > 1e-9)`, so informative.length > 0 and the abstain branch is skipped. The guard's own comment at L368-373 claims 'In week 1 every feature is zero', which was true before carryover was added.
defects.impact: This weekend (Week 1, 2026) the endpoint emits leans built from a feature distribution the model never saw in training — every training row had a within-season efficiency gap, every Week 1 serve row has a continuity-weighted last-season one, scored with the same coefficients. The documented protection against exactly this ('the honest output for no information is no pick') has been silently defeated. It also activates the rosterContinuity leak: contOf at L206 calls rosterContinuity(t, season), which for any historical replay of weeks 1-4 uses the 2026 roster as the continuity denominator for a past season.
defects.fix: Either train on week>=1 with the same carryover logic applied to training rows, or refuse to score weeks 1-4, or add a distinct carried_* feature so the coefficient is fitted on the quantity actually served.

defects.claim: The tempo coaching trait is labelled backwards: a genuinely slow team is reported as 'plays fast' and vice versa.
defects.evidence: The trait is defined at L193 as { key: 'off_seconds_per_drive', label: 'plays slowly', inverse: 'plays fast', flip: true }. Trace a genuinely slow team: high off_seconds_per_drive -> all.filter(x => x < v) is large -> pct ~= 0.9 -> flip makes pct = 0.1 -> the test `0.1 >= 0.75` is false -> t.inverse is selected -> 'plays fast'. The flip and the label/inverse pair double-invert because label/inverse were written against the UNflipped direction.
defects.impact: The reading string at L228 — the human-readable coaching summary shown to the user and quoted into pick explanations — asserts the opposite of the truth about tempo for every team outside the middle 50%. Note the flip is CORRECT for the numeric consumer (football-first.js:216 paceOf reads .percentile and needs high = fast), so removing the flip would break pace_edge.
defects.fix: Swap label and inverse for the off_seconds_per_drive entry at L193; leave the flip in place.

defects.claim: A live overtime game is reported at exactly 100% or 0% win probability, which the module's own code 15 lines later says it must never do.
defects.evidence: clockSeconds maps period 5+ (overtime) to 0 seconds remaining. liveWinProbability returns before ever reaching the clamp at L87-88 (`const floor = 0.005;`), whose comment at L84-86 reads: 'A game still being played is never 0% or 100%. The normal tail rounds to certainty long before football does ... Clamping keeps it from asserting an impossibility it has no basis for.' The comment at L92-93 says OT is 'treated as the dying seconds of a tied game', but 0 seconds is game over, not dying seconds.
defects.impact: A game currently being played in overtime with a 3-point lead returns exactly 1.0 (100%). The true figure is roughly 75-80% — after a field goal in OT the trailing team gets a possession. Mitigated only in that probability_reliable at L153 does evaluate to false for OT, so it is flagged even though the number itself asserts certainty about an undecided game.
defects.fix: Return a small positive remaining-time figure for overtime (e.g. 600 s for a 10-minute period, or a fixed nominal 300 s) so the clamp path is reached, rather than 0.

defects.claim: script_conflict carries the opposite sign from the file's own stated 'positive means home is advantaged' convention, so the decomposition narrates the mechanism backwards.
defects.evidence: L198-199 establishes 'Positive means the home side is advantaged, so every feature reads in one direction and a coefficient's sign is interpretable without a lookup.' L221 states 'spread is from the home team's view: positive means home is the underdog.' So spread > 3 means home is a 3+ point underdog, likely trailing, and a run-heavy home staff (low passOf) is forced out of its identity — a home DISadvantage. But `0.5 - passOf` is POSITIVE for a run-heavy staff, so the feature reads 'home advantaged'. The second term inverts identically.
defects.impact: Predictions are unaffected because the fitted coefficient absorbs a consistently flipped sign. But contributions[].points, leading_reason and leading_story at L391-411 then describe the causal mechanism backwards, and FEATURES[3].story at L111-112 states the intended direction. The entire selling point of the module (L356-358) is that 'the explanation is the decomposition rather than a story told afterwards'.
defects.fix: Negate both terms so the feature matches the stated convention, and refit.

defects.claim: Ridge regularisation is applied to unstandardised features, so the single lambda means something different for each column and the penalty is effectively arbitrary.
defects.snippet:
const lambda = 5;
for (let i = 1; i < p; i++) XtX[i][i] += lambda;   // intercept unpenalised
defects.evidence: The seven features live on incompatible scales: availability_edge is a usage share (~±0.3), pace_edge is a percentile difference in [-1,1], wind is (mph-15)/10, and qb_downgrade_edge is in POINTS and is documented at L125 as reaching 9.9. Ridge shrinks coefficients equally in absolute terms, so a feature measured in points has a naturally small coefficient and is barely penalised, while a feature measured as a share is crushed.
defects.impact: The relative shrinkage across features is set by an accident of units rather than by evidence, so the fitted coefficients — and therefore the reported per-feature contributions that constitute the whole output — are not comparable. The docstring at L249-251 claims the regularisation is principled ('not decoration: six correlated features on a few hundred games will happily produce large opposing coefficients that cancel'), which is true of ridge on standardised features but not of this.
defects.fix: Standardise each column to unit variance before forming XtX, fit, then un-standardise the coefficients; or scale lambda per column by that column's variance.

defects.claim: The connectivity audit scans only 3 of server/'s 11 code directories, so it can report a live module as orphaned dead weight and recommend deleting it.
defects.evidence: ls -d server/*/ returns betting/, data/, db/, draft/, migrations/, modeling/, news/, platform/, routes/, scripts/, services/ — eleven directories, of which the audit reads two plus index.js. Concretely, date-util.js is imported by server/betting/nfl/strategy/t60-runner.js (the live T-60 runner) and stats-util.js by server/modeling/candidates.js; neither import is counted toward importedBy.
defects.impact: A module used only from server/betting/, server/modeling/, server/db/, server/draft/, server/news/, server/platform/ or server/scripts/ is reported as ORPHANED, and the verdict string at L110-111 tells the reader to 'Wire them, list them as intentional, or delete them.' The note at L112-114 claims the analysis 'under-reports connectivity rather than over-reporting it — the safe direction', but under-reporting connectivity is precisely what produces a false delete recommendation.
defects.fix: Add every code-bearing directory under server/ to the record() sweep, recursing rather than reading a flat readdirSync.

defects.claim: ROOT is derived with URL.pathname, which is not a filesystem path; when it fails to resolve the audit silently reports healthy:true with zero modules scanned.
defects.snippet: const ROOT = new URL('../', import.meta.url).pathname;
defects.evidence: On Windows this yields '/C:/Users/...'; on any platform a path containing a space arrives percent-encoded as %20. Either way existsSync(SERVICES) is false, so jsFiles() returns [] at L42, services = [], orphans = [], unexpectedOrphans.length === 0, and L106-109 sets healthy: true with the verdict 'Every service module is either wired into the application or explicitly listed as deliberately unwired.'
defects.impact: A check whose entire purpose is finding dead code returns a clean bill of health when it cannot read a single file. This is the silent-success failure mode the module's own header (L6-14) was written to eliminate. Every other file in the repo already does this correctly — launcher.mjs:23, start.mjs:9, vite.config.ts:4 all use fileURLToPath.
defects.fix: Use fileURLToPath(new URL('../', import.meta.url)), and throw rather than return healthy when the services directory does not exist.

defects.claim: The offline guard that CI relies on to ENFORCE hermeticity is applied to the test step but omitted from the smoke step, which is the one that boots the real application.
defects.snippet:
- name: Fresh-install startup smoke test
        run: npm run start:smoke
        env:
          SCHEDULER_DISABLED: '1'
defects.evidence: The test step at L79-82 sets NODE_OPTIONS: '--import ./test/offline-guard.mjs' (I confirmed test/offline-guard.mjs exists) alongside SCHEDULER_DISABLED. The smoke step at L95-96 sets only SCHEDULER_DISABLED. The workflow header at L7-9 states it 'must never require provider credentials, call a paid data/LLM API, or activate real betting', and the test step's own comment at L68-73 explicitly rejects assertion-based hermeticity: 'that used to be the whole story, and it was an assertion about the suite rather than a property of the run -- a test that quietly reached a provider would have passed. The guard below ENFORCES it'.
defects.impact: npm run start:smoke boots the real server with its collectors and boot-time sync paths and nothing prevents an outbound call to a provider. SCHEDULER_DISABLED is a narrower guarantee than the guard, and it is the same assertion-rather-than-property posture the authors already rejected once for npm test.
defects.fix: Add NODE_OPTIONS: '--import ./test/offline-guard.mjs' to the smoke step's env block.

defects.claim: start.mjs exits with code 0 when the application failed to come online, so every wrapper reports a failed launch as success.
defects.snippet: server.on('exit', code => process.exit(code ?? 0));
defects.evidence: At L134-139 the failure path does `server.kill('SIGTERM'); process.exitCode = 1; return;`. Killing by signal fires the exit handler with code === null and signal === 'SIGTERM', so `code ?? 0` evaluates to 0 and process.exit(0) runs immediately — before the process.exitCode = 1 assignment on the preceding line can have any effect.
defects.impact: After 60 failed readiness probes the script tells the shell everything is fine. mac/Start Gridiron HQ.command, windows/Start Gridiron HQ.cmd and the generated Desktop shortcuts all wrap npm start and cannot distinguish a dead app from a healthy one; any CI or supervisor that checks the exit code is equally blind.
defects.fix: Capture the signal argument: server.on('exit', (code, signal) => process.exit(code ?? (signal ? 1 : 0))), and track whether the kill was the intentional failure path.

defects.claim: /status reports tunnel_up using the generic pgrep pattern that this same file documents as always matching the launcher's own permanent tunnel, so the field is hard-wired true.
defects.snippet: res.end(JSON.stringify({ server_up: portOpen(APP_PORT), tunnel_up: processRunning('cloudflared tunnel'), tunnel_url: tunnelUrl }));
defects.evidence: L82-86 states that 'cloudflared tunnel' 'also matches the launcher's own permanent tunnel (a different port, started once by launchd and always up), so that generic check always found *something*'. startTunnel at L89 was fixed to use the port-specific pattern; /status was not. ps confirms the launcher's own tunnel is running as PID 86537 (cloudflared tunnel --url http://127.0.0.1:5199), a permanent launchd service.
defects.impact: tunnel_up is always true and conveys no information. It is the field a phone user checks to find out whether the app's tunnel is up, and it says yes even when — as right now — the app's tunnel registrar is dead.
defects.fix: Use the same port-specific pattern as startTunnel, or derive it from whether tunnel_url is non-null.

defects.claim: The 'unrecoverable' regex matches the bare substring 'chain' anywhere in an error message, so a transient failure can permanently seal a preregistered audit designed to resume.
defects.snippet:
const unrecoverable = /no remaining weeks|already complete|sealed as|chain/i.test(message);
if (unrecoverable) failBlindAudit(auditId, error);
defects.evidence: The alternation is unanchored, so 'chain' matches inside 'markov chain', 'chained promise', 'certificate chain', or a Node TLS error code containing CHAIN. The comment immediately above at L232-236 records that this exact class of mistake has already cost work: 'the audit is week-chained and resumes at next_ordinal, so the next invocation continues from the last sealed week (runs 9 and 10 lost 23 opened weeks to sealing here).'
defects.impact: A transient network or TLS error whose message happens to contain 'chain' calls failBlindAudit() and permanently seals an audit that was explicitly architected to resume from the last sealed week — destroying preregistered audit work, which is the one thing the audit registry exists to protect.
defects.fix: Anchor the patterns to full messages or match on typed error classes/codes rather than substring-testing free-text messages.

defects.claim: A SQLite rollback journal from a pre-migration backup of the live database is tracked in git, because the ignore glob misses the -journal suffix.
defects.snippet:
*.sqlite.bak
*.pre-migration-*.bak
defects.evidence: `git ls-files | grep -iE 'sqlite|server/data|\.env'` returns server/data.sqlite.pre-migration-2026-09-11T00-19-06-457Z.bak-journal as a tracked file. The pattern *.pre-migration-*.bak at L53 does not match the trailing '-journal'; the sibling 9.8 GB .bak file IS correctly ignored.
defects.impact: A live-database artefact is committed to the repository, and because package-release.mjs drives its copy from `git ls-files`, it also ships in every release zip. The file is only 1024 bytes so the data exposure itself is negligible, but .gitignore L8-11 and L25-27 show this seatbelt has already been patched twice — this is the third gap in it.
defects.fix: Add *.bak-journal, *.bak-shm and *.bak-wal to .gitignore and git rm --cached the tracked journal.

defects.claim: Two EXCLUDE entries are no-ops in the git path, making the exclude list look more protective than it is.
defects.snippet:
const top = rel.split('/')[0];
if (EXCLUDE.has(top) || EXCLUDE.has(rel)) continue;
defects.evidence: For a path like server/data/analyst-notes-2026.json, top is 'server', never 'data' — so the 'data' entry cannot fire on the paths it was plainly written for. 'client/dist' only matches a rel exactly equal to the string 'client/dist', which `git ls-files` never emits because it lists files rather than directories.
defects.impact: A reader auditing what the release ships trusts a list in which two of the nine entries do nothing. Combined with the walk() fallback (G13c-45), the appearance of protection is doing the work that real protection should.
defects.fix: Test with a path-prefix match (rel === entry || rel.startsWith(entry + '/')) instead of exact equality on the first segment.

defects.claim: rosterContinuity takes a season parameter but queries the CURRENT roster with no season filter, so historical calls compare past usage against today's roster.
defects.evidence: season is a parameter at L487 and is used for the prior-season usage query at L492 (`WHERE u.team = ? AND u.season = ?`, team, season - 1) but is absent from this roster query. players.team_id reflects the roster as of now, so rosterContinuity(team, 2023) compares 2022 usage against the 2026 roster. The module header at L12 claims 'Everything is CUTOFF-SAFE'.
defects.impact: Correct for live use (season = 2026 today). Wrong for any replay of a past season, where a player who joined the team in 2025 is counted as 'retained' from 2022 — future information in a feature. Reached via football-first.js:206 contOf(), which fires only on the carryover path (weeks 1-4); fitResidualModel filters week>=5 so the fit itself is unaffected, but scripts/audit-football-first.mjs, weekly-walkforward.js and forward-ledger.js all score arbitrary weeks.
defects.fix: Either add an as-of-season roster source, or rename to currentRosterContinuity and throw when season !== the current season.

defects.claim: cachedAsync has no in-flight deduplication, so concurrent misses on the same key all execute the expensive fetch.
defects.evidence: Between the store.get miss and the store.set at L93 there is an await boundary during which any number of further requests observe the same miss and each call compute(). The synchronous cached() at L74-85 cannot exhibit this because it never yields.
defects.impact: For the fetch-backed computations this variant exists for, N concurrent requests produce N upstream calls — a thundering herd against a rate-limited or paid endpoint, plus N times the latency, in a module whose entire premise is eliminating redundant work.
defects.fix: Keep a Map of in-flight promises keyed by key+print; on a miss, store the promise before awaiting and have subsequent callers await the same one.

defects.claim: The 'lint' script and the CI step named 'Lint' perform only a syntax parse and verify nothing semantic.
defects.snippet:
for (const file of files) execFileSync(process.execPath, ['--check', file], { stdio: 'inherit' });
console.log(`Syntax checked ${files.length} JavaScript files; TypeScript/TSX is covered by npm run typecheck.`);
defects.evidence: node --check parses a file and exits; it performs no semantic analysis. It cannot detect an undefined variable, an unused binding, an unawaited promise, a shadowed name, == vs ===, an unreachable branch, a typo'd property, or an unresolvable import specifier. package.json:5 sets type: module so .js is at least parsed as ESM, meaning the check is valid as far as it goes.
defects.impact: For a codebase with 261 tables, ~19 statistical estimators and money-adjacent output, 'lint passes' currently guarantees only that every file parses. Every defect in this audit passes it — including G13c-54, where a declared-but-never-read const (OUTCOME_COLUMNS) silently disabled a leakage guard and no-unused-vars alone would have caught it.
defects.fix: Adopt ESLint with at minimum no-unused-vars, no-undef, require-atomic-updates and import/no-unresolved, and keep node --check as a fast pre-pass.

defects.claim: The Anthropic API key is read with an echoing prompt, so a billable credential is displayed on screen and left in terminal scrollback.
defects.snippet:
const rl = readline.createInterface({ input: process.stdin, output: process.stdout });
key = (await rl.question('  Paste your Anthropic API key (optional): ')).trim();
defects.evidence: readline/promises' question() echoes input by default; there is no muted-output stream or keypress interception anywhere in the surrounding block (L74-82).
defects.impact: An sk-ant- key is visible to anyone looking at the screen and persists in scrollback, in tmux/screen buffers, and in any terminal session logging. The installer is the one place a first-time user is guaranteed to type it.
defects.fix: Mute the output stream during the prompt (intercept _writeToOutput or read raw keypresses), or accept the key only via the existing --key flag.

defects.claim: The 0600 mode on .env is ignored when the file already exists, so a re-run leaves a world-readable secrets file while printing that it is private.
defects.snippet:
fs.writeFileSync(ENV, next, { mode: 0o600 });
ok('Key saved to .env (git-ignored, never leaves this machine)');
defects.evidence: Node's writeFileSync applies the mode option only when creating the file; for an existing path it writes contents and leaves permissions untouched. The current .env happens to be -rw------- so this is latent rather than active on this machine.
defects.impact: Re-running the installer against an existing 644 .env rewrites the API key into it and reports 'never leaves this machine' while every local user can read it.
defects.fix: Call fs.chmodSync(ENV, 0o600) unconditionally after the write.

defects.claim: npm ls --depth=0 is used as a hard install gate, but it exits non-zero for extraneous and unmet peer dependencies, so it can abort a perfectly good install.
defects.snippet:
res = spawnSync(npm, ['ls', '--depth=0'], { cwd: ROOT, stdio: 'inherit', shell: IS_WIN });
if (res.status !== 0) die('One or more required packages are missing. Scroll up for the npm report.');
defects.evidence: npm ls returns a non-zero status for extraneous packages and unmet peer dependencies, not only for missing ones. package.json carries react, react-dom, react-router-dom, @tanstack/react-query and @vitejs/plugin-react in devDependencies, a set in which peer-range mismatches are routine.
defects.impact: die() terminates the installer at step 2 of 8, before the .env, build, seed and data pull, on a dependency tree that would have worked — and the message ('One or more required packages are missing') misdiagnoses the cause, sending the user hunting for a missing package that is installed.
defects.fix: Downgrade to a warning, or check for the specific required packages with require.resolve rather than trusting npm ls's exit status.

defects.claim: On an unexpected cloudflared exit the URL-clearing POST is aborted in flight, so the app keeps advertising a dead tunnel address.
defects.snippet: child.on('exit', code => { console.log(`cloudflared exited (${code})`); register(''); process.exit(code ?? 0); });
defects.evidence: register('') returns a promise and is not awaited; process.exit() runs synchronously on the very next expression, terminating the process before the fetch completes. The deliberate shutdown path at L77-81 does it correctly: `const shutdown = async () => { await register(''); child.kill('SIGTERM'); process.exit(0); }`.
defects.impact: Settings -> Phone access continues to display a trycloudflare.com address that no longer resolves, so the user's phone gets a connection error with no indication why — exactly the state the 30-second re-registration at L62-64 was added to prevent.
defects.fix: Make the exit handler async and await register('') before process.exit, mirroring shutdown().

defects.claim: Team-count snapping breaks ties toward the lower allowed count, so an 11-team league is priced as a 10-team league.
defects.evidence: The comparison is strict <, so when |n - total| equals |best - total| the earlier (smaller) entry is kept. ALLOWED_TEAM_COUNTS is [8,10,12,14,16] in ascending order, so total = 11 is equidistant from 10 and 12 and resolves to 10.
defects.impact: An 11-team league receives 10-team FantasyCalc values. Player values differ meaningfully between 10- and 12-team formats, and 12 is by far the more common shape, so snapping down is the wrong tiebreak for the module whose sole purpose is not mispricing leagues that differ.
defects.fix: Use <= so ties resolve upward, or break ties explicitly toward 12.

defects.claim: The comment states the arcsine transform stabilises variance at ~1/(4n), but the transform implemented has variance 1/n.
defects.evidence: The asymptotic variance of 2*asin(sqrt(p)) is 1/n; it is asin(sqrt(p)) without the factor of 2 whose variance is 1/(4n). The factor of 2 is present in the code at L28, and the stated range [0, pi] confirms it.
defects.impact: No numeric effect — k is empirically fitted in shrinkage-fit.js — but anyone deriving a k prior analytically from this comment is off by a factor of 4.
defects.fix: Correct the comment to 1/n.

defects.claim: normalCdf is duplicated verbatim from stats-util.js rather than imported, and the two copies disagree at x === 0.
defects.evidence: stats-util.js:248-254 is the same Abramowitz-Stegun 7.1.26 implementation, and this module does not import it. stats-util uses `x >= 0` at L253 where this uses `x > 0` at L44. stats-util.js:218-219 makes a point of centralising its copula helpers 'so there is exactly one implementation of it'.
defects.impact: Two copies of one numeric routine drift independently; the edge-case divergence is harmless today (both yield ~0.5 at zero) but it is the shape of a future inconsistency.
defects.fix: Import normalCdf from ./stats-util.js and delete the local copy.

defects.claim: The replacement-quarterback cache is module-level and never invalidated, so the value freezes for the process lifetime while its source table keeps growing.
defects.evidence: Keyed on `${season}:${week}` only, with no fingerprint and no eviction. The live server (PID 56651) has been up since 2026-09-11 and syncs nfl_player_week_features continuously.
defects.impact: replacementQb(2026, 2) computed on the first call is still served after a full day of new player-week rows, so quarterbackPicture's downgrade_points drifts from the data. This is exactly what compute-cache.js exists to prevent, and this module does not use it.
defects.fix: Replace with cached() from compute-cache.js, fingerprinted on nfl_player_week_features.

defects.claim: The rebuild-staleness check omits two files that materially change the client build, so editing either serves a stale interface silently.
defects.evidence: client/tailwind.config.js and client/postcss.config.js both exist and both feed the build — the custom `field: '#1a4d2e'` theme colour lives in the former, and the latter wires tailwind into PostCSS. Neither path is in the Math.max set.
defects.impact: Changing a theme colour or the PostCSS plugin chain leaves builtMtime >= sourceMtime, so start.mjs skips the rebuild and serves the previous dist/ — the precise stale-build failure the surrounding comment at L41-45 says this function exists to catch.
defects.fix: Add both config paths to the Math.max call.

defects.claim: The missing_team_vector_repair phase is a byte-identical duplicate of team_feature_vectors.
defects.evidence: L149-152 calls backfillTeamFeatureVectors with exactly the same seasons, startWeek and endWeek; the only difference is the phase name string passed to recordProgress.
defects.impact: Either it is a no-op second full pass over every team-week (wasted time on an already long rebuild) or it was intended to target only missing rows and silently does not, in which case the repair it is named for never happens.
defects.fix: Either delete the phase or pass an onlyMissing option and implement it.

defects.claim: Two tables are created directly by a script, outside the migration system.
defects.evidence: nfl_rebuild_checkpoints and nfl_rebuild_progress (L41-45) are created here with no corresponding file in server/migrations/, unlike every other table in the 261-table database.
defects.impact: Schema tooling, migration-based audits and a fresh install have no record of these tables; their shape can only be learned by reading this script, and any change to it silently diverges from whatever already exists on disk.
defects.fix: Move both CREATE TABLE statements into a numbered migration.

defects.claim: withRandomSeed restores the global RNG in a finally block, so it silently fails to seed anything if fn is asynchronous.
defects.evidence: If fn returns a promise, the try block completes at the first await inside fn and finally restores rng immediately, long before the async work draws its random numbers. The docstring says 'Runs one synchronous simulation', but nothing enforces it.
defects.impact: An async caller gets a silently unseeded run that still reports as reproducible — the worst failure mode for a determinism helper used by regression tests and replays.
defects.fix: Throw if fn() returns a thenable, or provide an explicit async variant that awaits before restoring.

defects.claim: Table and column names are interpolated directly into SQL with no identifier validation.
defects.evidence: Every current call site passes a hard-coded string literal, so this is not presently exploitable; there is no allow-list or regex check on name or stamp anywhere in the function.
defects.impact: One fingerprint([req.query.table]) away from being a SQL injection point in a module imported by three route files.
defects.fix: Validate both against /^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$/ or an explicit allow-list before interpolating.

defects.claim: footballContext advertises a cutoff window of weeks 1..week-1 but the underlying functions read only the trailing 4 and 6 weeks.
defects.snippet: cutoff: `usage and tendencies from weeks 1..${week - 1}; injury report is pre-kickoff and not a leak`,
defects.evidence: availabilityPicture queries `week < ? AND week >= ?` with Math.max(1, week - lookback) and lookback = 4 (L90, L97); quarterbackPicture uses lookback = 6 (L340, L344).
defects.impact: The self-describing provenance field — the thing a reader trusts to know what went into a number — overstates the evidence window. Safe in the leakage direction (narrower, not wider), but wrong.
defects.fix: Report the actual windows, e.g. weeks ${Math.max(1, week-4)}..${week-1} for usage and ${Math.max(1, week-6)}..${week-1} for quarterback.

defects.claim: r_squared is computed against an uncentred total sum of squares and then reported to the user as a percentage explained.
defects.snippet: const ssTot = samples.reduce((s, x) => s + x.y * x.y, 0);
defects.evidence: This is sum(y^2), not sum((y - ybar)^2). The result is used at L311 as `r_squared: r3(1 - ssRes / ssTot)` and surfaced at L413 as `The fit explains ${((m.r_squared ?? 0) * 100).toFixed(1)}% of the market's residual.`
defects.impact: For a market residual ybar is near zero so the two are close, but the reported figure is not conventional R^2 while being presented as one in user-facing prose.
defects.fix: Centre y before computing ssTot, or rename the field to make the uncentred definition explicit.

defects.claim: The import-detection regexes miss side-effect imports and collide on basenames.
defects.snippet:
for (const m of src.matchAll(/from\s+['"]([^'"]+)['"]/g)) out.add(basename(m[1]));
for (const m of src.matchAll(/import\(\s*['"]([^'"]+)['"]/g)) out.add(basename(m[1]));
defects.evidence: Neither pattern matches `import './x.js'` (a side-effect import with no from clause) — scripts/fanduel-lines.mjs:15 uses exactly that form. The first pattern also fires on the word 'from' inside comments and string literals. Keying on basename alone makes ../db/index.js and any services/index.js the same key.
defects.impact: Under-counts real imports (feeding the false-orphan verdict of G13c-25) while over-counting spurious ones from prose.
defects.fix: Match the full ESM import grammar including side-effect form, and key on a resolved path rather than a basename.

defects.claim: The CSV insert loop runs outside any transaction, one statement per row.
defects.snippet:
run(insert,
    sourceGameKey, eventKey, r.season, r.date, r.time_est, r.away_team, r.home_team,
defects.evidence: No BEGIN/COMMIT anywhere in the file; run() is called once per parsed CSV row inside the for loop at L99-131.
defects.impact: Each insert is its own implicit transaction with its own fsync, making a multi-thousand-row import far slower than necessary, and a crash mid-run leaves a partially imported file. Mitigated by the deterministic source_game_key primary key with INSERT OR REPLACE, which makes a re-run idempotent.
defects.fix: Wrap the loop in a single transaction.

defects.claim: A legacy unshrunk fit with maximum weight k=1 is reported as low confidence with a reason that misstates why.
defects.evidence: nfl-expert-coordinator.js:302 falls back to `{ k: 1, reason: 'legacy fit: unshrunk' }` with no independent_weeks field, so independentWeeks arrives undefined and this branch fires despite k being at its maximum.
defects.impact: Direction is conservative and defensible, but the stated reason asserts there is no evidence when in fact the legacy fit simply did not record the count — a materially different claim to show a user weighing a pick.
defects.fix: Distinguish 'not recorded' from 'zero' and emit a reason naming the legacy fit.

defects.claim: percentiles() hard-codes rounding to one decimal place, which destroys any quantity smaller than 0.1.
defects.snippet: Object.fromEntries(qs.map(q => [`p${Math.round(q * 100)}`, +(quantile(a, q) ?? 0).toFixed(1)]));
defects.evidence: Operator precedence is correct — (quantile(a,q) ?? 0).toFixed(1) then unary + — so the only issue is the fixed scale. The default quantiles [0.05, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.95] suggest fantasy-point distributions, where 1 dp is appropriate.
defects.impact: Fine for its apparent intended use, but a probability array passed here returns p05 = 0.1 for a true 0.05 — a 100% error in a general-purpose exported helper with 37 importing modules.
defects.fix: Accept a precision parameter defaulting to 1.

dead_or_duplicate.reason: One-off rebuild script, now stale: hard-codes SEASONS = [2022, 2023, 2024, 2025] at L24 and 'season BETWEEN 2022 AND 2025' at L213-214 and L218-219, while it is now the 2026 season. It also creates two tables outside the migration system (L37-45) and contains a duplicate phase (L154-157).

One-off vendor CSV importer with no npm script and no importers, but it holds the P1 leakage fix (OUTCOME_COLUMNS is dead code) and the table it populates is live. Fix before archiving, so the next run does not re-introduce the leak.
normalCdf at L39-45 duplicates stats-util.js:248-254 byte-for-byte, in a file that does not import stats-util, contradicting stats-util.js:218-219's stated goal of a single implementation.
dead_or_duplicate.target: server/services/stats-util.js

dead_or_duplicate.reason: Not dead, but the name overstates it: node --check is a parse gate, not a linter, and the CI step is labelled 'Lint'. Keep as a fast pre-pass and supplement with a real linter rather than relying on it.

Reachable only via a dynamic import at server/routes/betting-hub.js:720, so not orphaned — but docs/reference/architecture/folder-map.csv:624 already proposes moving it to server/platform/utils/system-connectivity.js as a shared platform service, which matches its content (no domain logic).
dead_or_duplicate.target: server/platform/utils/system-connectivity.js

wiring.mechanism: spawn(NODE_BIN, ['--env-file-if-exists=.env', 'server/index.js'], { cwd: ROOT, detached: true, stdio: ['ignore', out, out] }) at L75-77, then child.unref(). defects.evidence: EventPanel's docstring at book_lag_lab.py:264-268 states filled is 'for use only in cross-sectional FEATURES ... never to invent a move that was not actually observed'. When the book has no row at step j, filled[book][j] returns its own row from up to MAX_FORWARD_FILL_STEPS=3 steps earlier (often `own` itself), so delta=0 and moved=0. Measured base move rate is 0.0071-0.0107 (server/data/book-lag-lab/latest.json next_move.*.base_move_rate), so these fabricated zeros sit inside the majority class of a rare-event target. FEATURE_KEYS_T1 (:416-417) includes own_steps_since_move and coverage - the model can lower log loss by learning 'this book is stale and thinly covered, so the forward-filled label reads 0', which is a statement about our polling cadence, not the market. research/test_book_lag_lab.py:62-69 appears to guard this invariant but asserts it on panel.moves (which correctly uses `observed`) and never exercises target1_rows.

defects.claim: The declared Level-1 objective is a sum of squared errors; the implemented objective is a mean. The ridge penalty is therefore ~n times stronger relative to the preregistered form, and the declared ALPHA_GRID does not mean what the preregistration says.
defects.snippet: return float(np.mean(resid ** 2) + alpha * np.sum(b ** 2))
defects.evidence: declaration() at :600 freezes into preregistered.json: 'min_b sum(y - Pb)^2 + alpha*sum(b^2) s.t. b >= 0, sum(b) = 1. Adopted verbatim from docs/MODEL_ARCHITECTURE_ASSESSMENT_2026_09_08.md part 2.6.' The module docstring at :12 and research/README.md:157 restate the same SUM form. Only simplex_ridge's own docstring at :135 is correct ('||y - Pb||^2/n'). With ALPHA_GRID = [0.0, 0.001, 0.01, 0.1, 1.0, 10.0] (:114) on an 831-row council fold, alpha=0.01 under the mean form is equivalent to alpha=8.31 under the declared sum form.
defects.impact: Anyone reconstructing the experiment from the frozen preregistration builds a materially different estimator. The negative result survives (market_only can take weight 1.0 at any alpha), but the preregistration is not a faithful description of what ran.
defects.fix: Change the declaration text (and the module docstring and README) to the /n form that the code implements, or divide alpha by n in the objective.

defects.claim: The totals quantile branch publishes a key-number push-mass block computed from spread MARGINS, not from game totals, labelled as if it described the totals market.
defects.snippet: margins = [abs(r['actual_margin']) for r in rows]
defects.evidence: key_number_push_mass always keys off actual_margin, and run_quantile calls it unconditionally at :932 ('key_mass = key_number_push_mass(train)') then publishes it at :950 as 'key_number_push_mass_train'. run() invokes run_quantile for both markets at :1021. Verified in server/data/tree-lab/latest.json: the totals 2025 quantile block reports margin 3 with share 0.1569 and spike_ratio 3.3824 - the same kind of number as the spreads block (0.1548, 3.2647). For a totals contract the meaningful push mass sits at total scores like 37/41/44/51, none of which is measured anywhere.
defects.impact: A reader of the totals quantile section is shown a spread diagnostic presented as belonging to totals. Secondary issue: KEY_NUMBERS (:82) includes 1, 2, 4 and 6, whose spike_ratio is contaminated by the neighbour average (margin 4 reports 0.427 and margin 2 reports 0.483 only because 3 is their neighbour), reported as though they were anti-spikes.
defects.fix: Make key_number_push_mass market-aware - use abs(actual_margin) for spreads and actual_total for totals, with a totals key list (37, 41, 44, 47, 51) - or omit the block from the totals branch.

defects.claim: hawkes_feasibility contradicts itself: its own computed criterion returns would_be_feasible: true while the prose verdict rendered in the UI hard-codes a no-go that ignores that flag, and the docstring's two stated reasons are contradicted by the module's own measurements.
defects.snippet:
'verdict': ('Not attempted. ' +
            f'{r4((fallback_share or 0) * 100)}% of book_updated_at stamps equal our own poll time exactly '
            ...
            f'roughly {moves_per_param} moves per parameter. Fitting one now would overfit a single week of '
defects.evidence: The criterion at :845-846 is `fallback_share < 0.15 and total_moves >= 5 * params_needed`. On the real data (server/data/book-lag-lab/latest.json hawkes_feasibility): fallback_share 0.0861 < 0.15 and total_confirmed_moves_all_books 1922 >= 5*110 = 550, so the frozen report carries "would_be_feasible": true alongside the no-go prose. The module docstring's reasons fail on the same numbers: :62-65 claims a 'meaningful share' of rows carry fetch-time fallback (measured 8.6%, below the module's own 15% bar) and :69-71 claims 'the number of genuine moves per book this week is in the single digits to low tens' (measured 1922/11 = ~175 per book). README.md:47-48 advertises this as 'checked fresh every run ... not assumed'. ResearchLab.tsx:203 renders hawkes_verdict.
defects.impact: A go/no-go the docs present as data-driven is overridden by a hard-coded assumption, and the UI shows a justification whose two premises the same object disproves.
defects.fix: Build the verdict string from would_be_feasible and the measured values, or raise the declared bar to whatever actually justifies declining and say so.

defects.claim: Opportunity routing is degenerate - every opportunity lands in one bucket because the survival input is a single per-market scalar - and that scalar is an extrapolation through a poll gap 12x longer than the decision horizon.
defects.snippet:
state = ('paper_opportunity' if survival >= thresholds['paper_opportunity']
                             else 'refresh' if survival >= thresholds['refresh'] else 'watch')
defects.evidence: survival is read once per panel at :801 as t3['delay_survival'].get('30', {}).get('survival_probability') and never varies by opportunity. The frozen values are 0.9997 (spreads) and 0.9986 (totals), both far above the 0.70 paper_opportunity threshold at :794, so server/data/book-lag-lab/latest.json opportunity_routing.counts is {'paper_opportunity': 8904} with zero refresh and zero watch. That 30s figure carries extrapolated: true on the same object - it is a constant-hazard fit projected through a measured 360.221s median poll gap. The 8904 count is also one entry per (leader-move, follower) pair, so a single stale follower is recounted once per book that moved ahead of it. ResearchLab.tsx:206 renders these counts as headline chips with no denominator.
defects.impact: A three-state execution router that has never emitted two states, driven entirely by a modelling assumption about a horizon never observed, is displayed as if it were a measurement of 8,904 real opportunities.
defects.fix: Make survival opportunity-specific (condition the hazard on gap size, book and time to kickoff), and report the routing count with its denominator and its distinct-follower count.

defects.claim: Baseline losses are computed in-sample on all rows while the candidate models are scored out-of-fold, and the two are then placed in one candidates dict and compared with min().
defects.evidence: base_rate is the empirical mean of the full labelled cell and base_pred is scored against that same y_move, whereas logit_cv and hgb_cv at :571-572 come from group_kfold_eval (GroupKFold on event_key). They are then merged into candidates_prob at :605-607 and selected with min() at :611, and both appear side by side in trials.json and in the published candidates block. The identical pattern applies to marginal_hazard_by_step at :687-689, which is fitted per step on all rows and scored on all rows.
defects.impact: The published candidate tables invite a direct comparison between an in-sample number and an out-of-fold number. The bias favours the baseline, so it does not manufacture the 'models win' result - but the margins quoted (0.0421 vs 0.0227 etc.) are not apples to apples.
defects.fix: Compute both baselines inside group_kfold_eval - fit the marginal rate / per-step hazard on each training fold and score it on the held-out fold.

defects.claim: Reads the live database without the snapshot transaction its sibling labs use and its own shared module calls a correctness property, and interpolates the path raw instead of via as_uri().
defects.snippet:
conn = sqlite3.connect(f'file:{db_path}?mode=ro', uri=True)
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    rows = conn.execute("""
defects.evidence: market_lab.py:72-74 and tree_lab.py:136-138 both issue con.execute('BEGIN') immediately after connecting, and research/betting/nfl/dataset.py:89-100 documents why: 'BEGIN because the live collector may be writing while this reads -- without it, two queries in the same build can see different states of the world and produce a dataset that never existed at any instant.' load_council has no BEGIN. It also builds the URI by f-string rather than Path(db_path).resolve().as_uri(), so a path containing ? or # is mis-parsed as URI syntax.
defects.impact: The consistency guarantee the other two labs advertise is absent in the lab that reads the largest table (nfl_weekly_expert_examples, 28,723 rows across 7 audit runs). Exposure today is limited because it is a single SELECT, but it is exactly the kind of divergence the shared module was written to eliminate.
defects.fix: Use dataset.read_only_connection(db_path), which does both correctly.

defects.claim: atomic_json here permits NaN where both sibling labs forbid it, so a NaN would serialize as an invalid-JSON bare token and silently remove the whole Package F section from the Research Lab page.
defects.snippet: tmp.write_text(json.dumps(value, indent=2, sort_keys=True, default=str))
defects.evidence: market_lab.py:57 writes json.dumps(value, indent=2, allow_nan=False) and book_lag_lab.py:166 writes json.dumps(value, indent=2, allow_nan=False, default=str). Python's default allow_nan=True emits bare NaN/Infinity, which JSON.parse rejects. nfl-research-lab.js:16 wraps the parse in try/catch and returns null, and :121-122 then yields expertSelectorLab = null, so the UI renders 'No saved selector experiment yet' (ResearchLab.tsx:261) rather than an error. Plausible NaN sources: mae()/mse() on an empty slice, and float(np.std(P[i][mask[i] > 0])) at :344 when a row has one available expert.
defects.impact: A silent disappearance of a completed negative result rather than a loud failure. No NaN is present in the current file - I checked - but the guard that would make that guaranteed is missing.
defects.fix: Add allow_nan=False to the json.dumps call at :122.

defects.claim: The shared cutoff-safe chronology module is orphaned: nothing imports it, so the duplication it was written to remove is still live in both labs and still listed as a limitation in every published tree-lab report.
defects.snippet:
Two copies of a chronology is two chronologies. They agree today because
someone kept them in step by hand; the first time one is fixed and the other is
not, two experiments quietly stop being comparable, and nothing fails.
defects.evidence: market_lab.py's imports (:17-32) and tree_lab.py's imports (:52-70) contain no reference to it; grep -rn 'betting' research/*.py returns one unrelated docstring hit at tree_lab.py:519. The only importer is research/betting/nfl/test_dataset.py:23, reached via sys.path.insert at :20-21. tree_lab.py:41-50 still carries the copy-paste comment and tree_lab.py:991-993 still publishes 'This dataset builder duplicates (rather than imports) market_lab.build_dataset's chronology block ... the two extractors must be kept in agreement by hand' in every report, including server/data/tree-lab/latest.json:137. docs/CLAUDE-NEXT-STEPS.md:87 records slice 6 as implemented.
defects.impact: The plan's slice 6 is recorded as done, the module exists and is correct, and the risk it was written to close is unchanged. Any future fix to one lab's chronology still silently desynchronizes the two experiments.
defects.fix: Import dataset.shared_setup in both build_dataset functions. First add a `limit` parameter to features_before so it can reproduce the labs' 8-week mean (see D-28).

defects.claim: The consumer-parity test does not test parity with the labs - it re-types their chronology inline, creating a third copy that will keep passing after a lab changes.

# Recompute the labs' own inline chronology, exactly as both files
            # write it today, and require identical output.
            con = sqlite3.connect(Path(db).resolve().as_uri() + '?mode=ro', uri=True)
defects.evidence: The method is named test_market_lab_and_tree_lab_agree_with_the_shared_chronology (:159) and the class docstring says 'The extraction must reproduce what the labs already compute' (:156-157), but the body at :171-188 hand-copies the SELECT, the 3-day lag, the week_end max and the history append rather than calling market_lab.build_dataset or tree_lab.build_dataset. defects.claim: latest.json is unconditional 'newest wins' with no record of superseded runs, and the published run happens to be the only one of three on the identical dataset whose pooled totals ROI is positive.
defects.snippet: def save():atomic_json(run_dir/'report.json',report);atomic_json(out/'latest.json',report)
defects.evidence: server/data/market-lab/ holds three completed runs with identical dataset_hash c0067d19...: 20260908T152001Z-7f69ded8 (totals selections no_move/extra_trees/no_move, pooled ROI -28.6%), 20260908T152747Z-7f69ded8 (byte-identical code_hash, identical results), and 20260908T152845Z-334b4b45 (selections tpot/tpot/no_move, pooled ROI +2.0%) which is latest.json. Mitigating: runs 1 and 2 had TPOT crash on every fold (report.json errors show XGBoostError/libomp and ModuleNotFoundError: pkg_resources), so run 3 is an environment fix, not result shopping. The report carries no supersedes field, so a reader of latest.json cannot tell.
defects.impact: A reader of the published report cannot see that two prior complete runs of the same preregistered protocol on the same data exist and reported a pooled totals ROI of the opposite sign.

defects.claim: The ranker and market-anchored logit branches filter training rows by season only, skipping the settled-label cutoff every other branch applies.
defects.snippet: train_c = [r for r in cover_rows if r['season'] < 2025]
defects.evidence: run_movement:749, run_classification:805 and run_quantile:895 all apply 'and stamp(r['label_at']) < outer_cutoff' on top of the season test. The ranker's train_final at :1035 and the logit's train_c at :1045 apply only the season test. research/betting/nfl/dataset.py:238-240 names this exact omission as 'the common mistake: it keeps a game from an earlier season whose label settled after the decision being scored, which looks chronological and is not.'
defects.impact: No actual leak results (the 2024 season settles in January, 2025 opens in September), but two of the report's branches carry a weaker guarantee than the other three and nothing says so.
defects.fix: Apply fold_cutoff / the outer_cutoff filter to train_final and train_c.

defects.claim: Finiteness is validated on the training slice only, so a leaking column with a non-finite value in a validation slice scores NaN and is silently never flagged.
defects.snippet:
if not np.isfinite(xt).all() or np.unique(xt).size < 2:
            continue
defects.evidence: xv is never checked in _fold_r2 (:37-45) or _fold_auc (:52-60). A NaN in xv produces NaN predictions, r2_score returns NaN, np.mean returns NaN, and the flag test at :91 ('score >= r2_threshold') evaluates NaN >= 0.98 as False. The resulting NaN in the features list would then be rejected by market_lab.atomic_json's allow_nan=False at :57, crashing the save rather than mis-reporting - so the loud half is covered and the silent-skip half is not.
defects.impact: The scanner can miss a genuine leak and the run either crashes at write time or records a null score, neither of which reads as 'this column could not be checked'.
defects.fix: Validate np.isfinite(xv).all() alongside xt, and record an explicit skipped_reason per feature instead of a None/NaN score.

defects.claim: graded_ranking reports full power on a fold with no grade separation: if every label is equal, every row counts as top-grade.
defects.snippet:
top = float(np.sum(y >= (float(np.max(y)) - 1e-9))) if rows else 0.0
        raw = top
defects.evidence: With y all zeros, max(y) == 0 and the comparison is true for every row, so raw == rows and effective_n is the full cluster-discounted row count. Compare the continuous_regression branch at :316-318, which explicitly handles the constant label ('the label is constant across the fold; there is nothing to predict') and returns 0.0. tree_lab.run_ranker:625 can produce an all-equal grade vector for a week whose profits are all identical.
defects.impact: A ranking fold that carries no ordering information at all would pass its observation-to-parameter check at full strength.
defects.fix: Mirror the continuous branch: if np.max(y) == np.min(y), set raw = 0.0 with a basis explaining there is no grade separation.

defects.claim: The test that stands for 'every lab runs the discipline check' asserts only that a string appears in each lab's source, so it passes while zero frozen reports contain a model_discipline block.
defects.evidence: See D-01: model_discipline is absent from all four published reports. This test passes today. The same gap applies to drift.py, which has no equivalent test at all.
defects.impact: The test suite provides false assurance on the one property that turned out to be unmet.
defects.fix: Assert on a completed report fixture instead: run a lab against a small synthetic DB (as test_dataset.py does) and assert report['model_discipline']['checks'] > 0.

defects.claim: calibration_weak requires every role's reference to be weak, so a fold where only the market role is uncalibrated reports strong calibration.
defects.snippet: weak = all(bool(r.get('weak')) for r in reference.values())
defects.evidence: season_boundary_reference marks a role weak whenever it pooled fewer than 8 PSI observations (:335 vs :350). With tree_lab's 86 features the availability and model roles clear 8 easily while the market role (about 8 columns) may not. _verdict_for does carry the per-role weak into its prose at :544-546, so the information exists per feature - but the top-level flag, which is what the summary at :647-649 and ResearchLab.tsx:333 read, can be False while a role is running on the fallback noise floor.
defects.impact: A fold can present as fully calibrated while one role's verdicts rest on the analytic noise floor rather than an NFL season-boundary reference.
defects.fix: Report weak per role in the summary, and set calibration_weak with any() or expose a weak_roles list.

defects.claim: The report's first limitation hard-codes an event count that contradicts the measured one in the same report.

ResearchLab.tsx:191 renders panel_summary.events (44) while :210 renders this limitation string (48).

defects.claim: beats_market_log_loss is decided by a strict float comparison, so when the anchored logit selects shrinkage 0.0 (i.e. it IS the market) the report says the market fails to beat itself.
defects.snippet: 'beats_market_log_loss': ll < market_ll, 'paper_bets': len(bets),
defects.evidence: server/data/tree-lab/latest.json market_anchored_logit[0]: shrinkage_selected 0.0, log_loss 0.6939137339320574, market_log_loss 0.6939137339320572, beats_market_log_loss false. The 2e-16 gap is floating-point noise in sigmoid(logit(p) + 0*(...)) at :715. The same field is the headline of every cover candidate row.
defects.impact: The cleanest statement of the no-edge result in the suite - 'inner CV chose shrinkage 0, so take the market' - is presented as a failure rather than as the result it is.
defects.fix: Compare with a tolerance (ll < market_ll - 1e-9) and surface shrinkage_selected == 0 as its own explicit verdict.

defects.claim: The market-anchored logit's discipline verdict label omits the season, breaking the labelling convention every other verdict follows.

defects.evidence: Every other call uses f'{market}/{season}/{target}/{fold}' - run_movement:759,762; run_classification:825,828; run_quantile:906,910; run_ranker:636. This one carries only the market, so a reader of model_discipline.folds cannot tell which outer window the verdict belongs to (it is always the 2025 test season, per :1038).

defects.claim: Family clustering is computed on every season except the last, so it uses seasons that the earlier walk-forward folds score.
defects.snippet:
train_mask = np.array([s != max(set(seasons)) for s in seasons])
    families, pairs = cluster_families(P[train_mask], mask[train_mask], columns)
defects.evidence: walk_forward's first fold (:480-483) trains on unique[:1] and scores unique[1], so for the council substrate it trains on 2022 and scores 2023 - a season included in train_mask. Impact is contained because families only drive family_ablation, and at FAMILY_CORRELATION = 0.90 every expert is a singleton (the report shows families: 18 for 18 columns, 7 for 7), which the code itself discloses at :781-782 ('family ablation below is equivalent to leave-one-expert-out and is reported as such rather than as a stronger test').

files.purpose: Operator docs for all four labs plus the leakage scanner; publishes the Package F negative result verbatim at :203-212.
files.note: Three stale claims: :117-118 says the leakage scan runs on every experiment (it covers 7 of ~14 target/market/season cells); the Package B section's 'roughly one hour' poll gap is measured at 360.2s; :8 documents --tpot-minutes 0.5 while the published run used 0.1.

files.purpose: Exact pins for the isolated research venv, each with a comment explaining why it exists.
files.note: The setuptools<81 pin is vindicated by market-lab run 2's frozen errors (ModuleNotFoundError: pkg_resources). joblib is imported directly by market_lab.py:29 and tree_lab.py:65 and is not listed - the same argument the file makes for scipy at :13-18.

files.purpose: Single-feature out-of-fold leak detector: flags any column whose univariate skill against the label is implausibly close to perfect (R2>=0.98 / AUC>=0.985), reusing the experiment's own chronological folds.
files.note: The guard IS real - it runs on real data, is proven against a synthetic leak, and found nothing (max observed R2 0.0091, max AUC 0.6025). But it is narrow by construction (its own docstring at :19-24 says so) and does not cover totals movement, the quantile target, the ranker or the logit branch. See D-05, D-11.

files.purpose: The pilot (Package C baseline): opening-to-closing movement regression, four families plus bounded TPOT, three outer seasons, expanding whole-week inner folds with a 7-day settled-label embargo.
files.note: Chronology guard block (:112-122) is careful and I found no path for post-decision data into a feature. Result: spreads no_move x3 zero bets; totals selected model significantly WORSE than no-move (gain CI [-0.0599,-0.0138]). Defects D-02 (TPOT selection bias), D-03 (no superseded-run record).

files.purpose: Pre-fit observation-to-parameter check with six target-specific numerators (rows / minority class / follow events / quantile tail mass / simplex free params / top-graded items) and a Kish design-effect discount from a per-fold ICC.
files.note: Best-argued module in the set (172-line docstring citing Peduzzi 1996, deriving the quantile numerator, and refusing PCA compression with reasons). Has NEVER produced a verdict in any frozen report - see D-01. Also D-12, D-13.

files.purpose: Distributional-drift scan: PSI against an analytic chi-square noise floor plus an empirical NFL season-boundary reference, normalized Wasserstein, role-aware verdicts, and a group-permuted domain classifier for PSI's marginal blind spot.
files.note: Rigorous and the best-tested module here (test_drift.py validates the analytic PSI null against a 400-draw empirical null and pins the tree-vs-linear domain classifier as a test). Has NEVER produced a scan in any frozen report - see D-01. Also D-14, D-15.

files.purpose: Package C extended: 86 features, three targets (movement / cover / residual quantile), 6+ families each plus a genuine market-only baseline, an LGBMRanker branch, a market-anchored logit branch, leakage + drift scans, and emit_oof for Package F.
files.note: Largest file in scope. Result is a clean negative (cover never beats the market log loss; quantile picks market_only 5/6; ranker ROI -16.8%/-9.2%; anchored logit selects shrinkage 0.0 = take the market). Defects D-04, D-05, D-09, D-16, D-17, D-18.

files.purpose: Package F: simplex-constrained (non-negative, sum-to-1) ridge stacker over experts with a mixture-of-experts gate on disagreement/coverage/week at 2 and 3 bins, benchmarked against market-only, static-equal-weight and the production coordinator.
files.note: Complete negative on all three substrates on both metrics; 7 configurations significantly WORSE than the market. Preregistration written before scoring (verified by timestamps), but D-08 (declared cover trial never run, never reported) and D-10 (declared objective is sum-of-squares, code is mean) are substantive gaps. Also D-19, D-20, D-21.

files.purpose: Package B: cross-book lead/lag from a frozen Package A evidence tape (never opens data.sqlite). Symmetric lead/lag map, next-move probability/size, time-to-follow hazard, delay survival, and watch/refresh/paper routing.
files.note: The only lab publishing a positive headline, and it does not survive inspection: D-06 (label built from forward-filled quotes, violating its own :264-268 invariant) and D-04b (verdict counts half-failing cells as passes). Also D-22, D-23, D-24, D-25, and dead cluster_interval at :193. Genuinely interesting side finding: Pinnacle has the LOWEST leader_share (0.355) of any readable book.

files.purpose: The extracted shared cutoff-safe chronology (read-only snapshot connection, 3-day publication proxy, strictly-earlier lookups, fold_cutoff, eligible_training_rows) that CLAUDE-NEXT-STEPS slice 6 asked for.

Listed keep/new_this_round_verified at docs/reference/architecture/folder-map.csv:211. See D-26, D-27, D-28 (features_before returns only the latest week while both labs average the last 8).

files.purpose: Settlement math including pushes and a None price; time_folds label purge and whole-week grouping; zero-prediction abstention.
files.note: Small but load-bearing - entry point via unittest discovery.

files.purpose: The injected-leak proof for leakage.py (regression and classification), quantile coherence detection, calibration coverage, key-number spike, no-vig probability, and digest/fold determinism.

files.purpose: Forward-fill staleness, sub-threshold move rejection, missing-quote-is-not-a-move, an AST check that no book name is hardcoded outside the docstring, hazard extrapolation direction, and the not-readable gate.

files.purpose: Validates the analytic PSI null against a 400-draw empirical null; proves the conventional 0.1 threshold false-alarms at these fold sizes; tests both directions (ordinary season shift NOT flagged, injected source change and dark feed flagged); pins the tree-vs-linear domain classifier choice as a test.
files.note: Strongest test file in the set. Tests code that has never run on real data (D-01).

files.purpose: Every target-type numerator, ICC/design-effect edge cases, all degenerate folds, strict-vs-report plumbing, and an AST authority check that the module contains no sqlite3/kelly/stake.
files.note: Weakened by :291-295, which asserts only that the string 'model_discipline' appears in each lab's source - see D-13.

files.purpose: Proves the simplex constraint holds, the blend cannot leave its experts' envelope even against a 1e6 haywire column, market_only can win outright, masking renormalizes rather than biasing toward zero, gate edges are training-only, and the expert drift scan flags a coverage collapse.

result.summary: The Python research lab is eight modules (~4,800 lines of source plus ~1,300 of tests) that run offline against a read-only SQLite snapshot and a frozen quote tape, and write versioned JSON reports that the Node app renders read-only on one Research Lab page. Nothing in it has staking authority, feeds a prediction, or writes to the database: nfl-research-lab.js is imported by exactly one route for one display endpoint, and the authority: research_only / production_changed: false fields in every report are accurate. The code is, on the whole, unusually honest research work — it preregisters before scoring, publishes negative results in its own README, names its proxies inline, and argues its methodological choices in docstrings rather than asserting them. The central structural finding is that several guarantees the suite advertises are not currently realized on disk. Every frozen report is schema -v1 while every lab on disk is -v2 with a different code_hash, so model_discipline.py (539 lines) and drift.py (704 lines) have never produced a single verdict in any published artifact and the UI panels that render them are permanently empty; the checks that would have caught other findings here simply did not run. The leakage guard is real — it executes on real data, reuses the experiment's own chronological folds, is proven against a synthetic injected leak, and found nothing (max single-feature out-of-fold AUC 0.60 against a 0.985 bar, max R2 0.0091 against 0.98) — but it is narrow by construction and covers 7 of roughly 14 fitted target cells, not "every experiment" as the README claims. Preregistration was honoured in ordering and form for all four labs, verified against the frozen timestamps and hashes, with two substantive gaps: a declared Package F trial (the tree cover substrate) was never run and never reported as un-run, though its six OOF files sit unopened on disk, and Package F's declared objective is a sum of squared errors while the code minimizes a mean, making the declared alpha grid mean something different than preregistered. The results themselves are three clean negatives — market-lab selects no_move outright on spreads and a significantly-worse-than-nothing model on totals, tree-lab never beats the market on cover log loss and its market-anchored logit selects shrinkage 0.0 (take the market), and expert-selector-lab fails its declared bar on every substrate with seven configurations significantly worse than the market — all consistent with the settled no-edge finding. The one positive headline, book_lag_lab's "8 of 8 cells beat their baseline", does not survive inspection: its verdict counts a cell as passing when only one of its two models won (the magnitude model lost all six), and its next-move label is built from forward-filled quotes, fabricating "no move" whenever a book was simply not quoted while the features encode exactly that staleness. Separately, TPOT is selected by an unfair comparison in both labs — its score is the maximum of a search over the very folds it is then scored on, compared by min() against unsearched fixed candidates — and it won 8 of 12 tree-lab cells then lost out of sample in 7, and in market-lab flipped the published pooled totals ROI from -28.6% to +2.0%. The extracted shared chronology module research/betting/nfl/dataset.py is correct and orphaned: nothing imports it, its parity test re-types the labs' logic rather than importing them, and the duplication it was written to remove is still published as a live limitation in every tree-lab report. The two fantasy JSONs are the only files here that reach a real decision, both via draft-assist.js, and draft-audit-signals-2026.json is the strongest artifact in the set — 2,182 matched player-seasons, actuals validated twice, nulls published alongside findings — and it documents a player_week_usage gsis crosswalk corruption that the suite's one holdout-confirmed positive result (role-scenario-lab's touches improvement, directly on Nick's fantasy-first priority) is built on and has not been checked against.

result.summary: I verified the status register in docs/CLAUDE-NEXT-STEPS.md claim by claim against the tree. It is substantially honest: all 18 named test files exist, all 10 named commit hashes resolve and their subjects match the corrections they are cited for, slices 7 and 8 really are unstarted (no spread-family-adapters.js, no lineup_lab.py/market_surface.py), and most "remaining limitation" cells are more pessimistic than the code warrants. The register's real failure is drift: it was last updated around 612361b/be51226 and roughly 19 commits of real work have landed since, so it no longer functions as the inventory sections 0 and 12 assign it. The largest divergence is that the Wong teaser product (2 services, 4 strategy modules, a route, 12 client files, 6 test files) was built after the plan and is the repo's only measured +EV, yet the plan mentions "teaser" zero times and its own scope companion FOLDER-REORGANIZATION.md:9,11 explicitly forbade building it. folder-map.csv holds 829 rows, not the claimed 820, and 34 tracked files at HEAD (31 of them the teaser/Wong/alt-spread work) have no row at all, so "covers every tracked file, none undisposed" is false. Slice 9's stated blocker ("nfl-research-lab.js still derives its root from ../..") was fixed at 56d67b9 and its required path test now exists, so a reader would skip work that is unblocked. C09's evidence column names a synthetic-fixture test while its headline run-27 reproduction lives in an unnamed file whose assertions are all skipped on a clean checkout. C05 claims 30 passing tests for a file that has had 20 then 26, never 30. Section 0.3 says the highest state reached is "connected" when 0.1 marks C12 observed and C03 installed and no row is "connected". Outside the plan, the root README and the governance manual both still headline Run 7's -16.952u/-11.77% as current when the DB holds completed runs 27, 31 and 32; domain-ownership.md calls itself definitive while classifying 202 of 270 services and omitting the entire nfl-execution path; and the manual asserts SCHEDULER_DISABLED is blocking capture when it is unset and the live tier is running. Two code findings fell out: a tracked 1KB SQLite backup journal committed against the plan's own section 10.4 that ships in the release zip, and a 1,654-line margin-distribution.js with zero importers whose comments twice cite a test file that has never existed in any commit. The docs are high quality and unusually honest about their limits; they are simply two to three weeks behind the tree on every number.

result.label: G20-docs-evidence
result.summary: This group is the project's entire written evidence record: 57 files, 17,818 lines, spanning the September 9/10/11 audit cycle, 28 relocated historical studies, three frozen contracts, two frozen fantasy baselines, and eight live fantasy reference docs. Almost nothing here is imported by runtime code — only three contract/reference files are — so the group's function is entirely epistemic: it is what a future agent reads to decide what is already known. Judged on writing quality it is exceptional; the docs routinely record their own retractions (WORK_LOG.md:457 retracting 0.813 to 0.289), their own introduced defects (CODEX-6-HANDOFF.md:427-442 and :464-485), and their own unverifiability (RETURN-TO-CODEX.md:193-213 stating four of five measurement claims have no stored artifact of any kind). Judged as a reference system it is messy and in places actively misleading. Three defects are P1. The archive-median opener backfill recorded at profitability-baselines.md:404-412 corrupted exactly seasons 2022-2025 — the odds archive's coverage minus 2026 (live ESPN openers) and minus 2021 (excluded by the backfill's own default season list) — which is precisely the antisymmetry signature RETURN-TO-CODEX.md:98-105 measured; no document connects the cause to the effect, and the backfill violates the project's own canonical rule OOF-1 clause 8. The shopping board, the one module built on the only claimed positive edge, drops most books by construction at nfl-shopping-board.js:92-94. The two frozen fantasy baselines carry byte-identical commit and dataset_hash yet different numbers, so the declared Build-Order 0.3 target "Fantasy MAE < 42.10" was never met (shipped 42.12) while STAGE_1_RESULTS.md:91 reports "model wins" because the comparator moved. Beyond those: the single most important betting number — the line-shopping edge — has five unreconciled values and its test is skipped in CI; "the historical blind audit" has six irreconcilable spread records; 97 doc references across 54 source files are broken against a handoff claim that only three needed updating; and .env does not contain SCHEDULER_DISABLED although three documents state it does and one carries a standing "do not re-raise this" instruction premised on it. Seventeen of 28 historical files lack the "not a work queue" banner, and two of those are live-voice work queues carrying literal code patches and a spending instruction. For the fantasy-first priority the fantasy reference docs are the best material in the repo, but the entire 2026 draft board rests on an ECR-to-ESPN rank substitution that PRESEASON_MODEL.md:406-409 says has never been validated, and two fantasy research candidates plus a time-critical, un-backfillable ADP-snapshot recommendation were never carried into the active plan.
