defects.claim: The argument used to withdraw the 4.26 max-z ceiling is numerically wrong: the 95% quantile for 4,060 independent one-sided tests is 4.21, not 4.44, and 4.26 is not the 99% quantile either.
defects.snippet: The previously quoted ceiling of **4.26 is suspect as a 95% quantile** — for 4,060 independent one-sided tests that quantile is 4.44, and positive correlation can only push it down, so 4.26 would imply more effective independent tests than were run. It is plausible as a 99% quantile.
defects.evidence: Computed: Sidak 95% max-z for m=4060 is 4.2124 (1-0.95^(1/4060) = 1.2634e-5), which must sit just below the document's own Bonferroni figure of 4.22 at the same line - and does. 4.44 corresponds to m ~ 11,400. The 99% quantile is 4.567; 4.26 is the 99% quantile for m ~ 983. 4.26 implies ~5,018 effective independent tests against 4,060 run - 24% more, a mild inconsistency rather than the impossibility claimed.
defects.impact: A document whose entire subject is whether this project's numbers can be trusted withdraws a figure using an incorrect calculation. The conclusion survives (max-z 2.87 < 4.21 under any reading) but the stated reasoning does not.
defects.fix: Replace 4.44 with 4.21 and restate the inference as 'consistent with roughly 5,000 effective independent tests, mildly more than were run'.

defects.claim: The project declares engines node >=22.5 and CI pins node-version '22' (.github/workflows/ci.yml:45), but the suite is only green on the developer's Node v25.9.0. Codex ran it on Node 22 against a copy of HEAD on 2026-09-11 and recorded 1,642 tests / 1,589 pass / 11 fail / 3 cancelled / 39 skipped, against commit 14c5e65's claimed 0 fail. All 11 failures are error 'Connection error.' with stacks through @anthropic-ai/sdk/core.mjs:330 -> callClaude (server/services/claude.js:118) — the mock.module('node-fetch', ...) interception used by test/page-explain.test.js:15-16 and test/nfl-news-events.test.js:11 did not take effect on Node 22, so the real Anthropic SDK fired. test/offline-guard.mjs only replaces globalThis.fetch and is loaded solely via NODE_OPTIONS in CI (ci.yml:81).
defects.impact: The declared and CI-pinned Node version fails 11 tests and cancels 3, so every 'N tests, 0 fail' figure in the commit bodies and in docs/CLAUDE-NEXT-STEPS.md describes Node 25 only without saying so. Worse, the failure mode of a version-fragile module mock is a live paid Anthropic call rather than a test error: a developer running plain npm test on a mock-incompatible Node with a key in the environment spends money silently. Evidence: Codex/2026-09-11/ok-x20/work/node22-tests.log:10428-10434, :6546-6560, :7958-7975.

result.summary: Read both transcripts end to end (7,330 + 9,435 events; 162 of Nick's own messages, ~800 assistant text blocks, 126 sub-agents). NOTE: session bfdb8e6f runs 2026-09-03 20:02Z to 2026-09-05 00:18Z, not Sep 3-8 as briefed. It is the betting-model audit continuation: it fast-forwarded a month-stale main over a 274-commit branch, fixed ~15 real bugs (worst: ESPN stat-id 44 aliased to "receptions", inflating every PPR score ~40% in all 6 leagues; an inverted MLB NRFI model where higher stated confidence won less often; a closing-line freeze bug that would have made every CLV comparison this season meaningless), built and validated the fantasy coordinator through 4 phases, then ran ~40 research agents whose unanimous conclusion was that there is no NFL betting prediction edge to find and the only proven edge is execution (line shopping, +2.57%/bet). Session 8346c03e (2026-09-06 19:00Z to 2026-09-08 15:04Z) is draft prep and the draft itself: phone pairing + tunnel + launchd launcher, a VORP rewrite of the draft ranker, forensics tracing Nick's ESPN logouts to Gridiron's own hourly roster job firing mid-draft with his live session cookie, the discovery that ESPN's REST draft view is frozen during a live draft (picks only flow over a WebSocket), and a bookmarklet-then-extension capture path that was still capturing zero frames at kickoff and got fixed live mid-draft (manifest missing fantasydraft.espn.com; WebSocket patched in the extension's isolated world instead of the page's MAIN world) plus a one-click Resync that backfilled the ledger. Verified in the DB: draft 20 holds 127 picks, 1 to 127, no gaps, all source espn-page. Seven candidate models were tested on draft day and six honestly declined; the one real win was recalibrating the preseason projection band (claimed 60% coverage, actually covered 69%). The session ends on an unanswered offer to write tests for the four emergency fixes; grep confirms none were ever written and the Chrome extension has zero test coverage.

result.label: H06-data-layer
nick_rules: Repo is read-only for this audit: never edit/create/delete inside fantasy-football-dashboard, never run state-changing git, never touch the live server (PID 56651, port 5177) capturing NFL Week 1 T-60 packets, never open server/data.sqlite except read-only via node:sqlite, never open .bak files, never call paid APIs
Every claim must be cited as path:line with a quoted snippet or it doesn't count as a defect
Big files must be read in full via chunked reads (lines_read == wc -l), not sampled -- applied here to sqlite queries covering literally all 261 tables rather than a sample
Nick's own memory/standing preference: fantasy over betting, betting engine is secondary -- corroborated independently by finding the nfl-execution domain (27 tables) holds only 1,004 total rows
App must stay running through 9/15 for live data capture (quoted from a prior session's summary of Nick's own note) -- respected by never restarting or stopping the process

Snapshots (.bak files) are deliberately never auto-pruned per the code's own comment: deleting a recovery point is a judgment call that belongs to a person who knows what's in it -- carried into this audit's cleanup plan by putting .bak deletion in the 'needs Nick's confirmation' tier, not the 'safe to do now' tier
result.summary: Full read-only inventory of the Gridiron HQ data layer: all 261 tables counted (25.25M rows total), sized via dbstat (7.33GB table data + 4.34GB indexes = 11.66GB, matching file size), grouped into 9 domains, cross-checked against code (grep) to find only 5 genuinely dead tables. Confirmed the tracked .bak-journal file's origin (an orphaned failed VACUUM INTO from commit 889dcf1) and proved the .gitignore gap that let it happen is still open today. Diagnosed the WAL bloat mechanism (no checkpoint-truncation code anywhere + live 1.27M-row/hour capture burst) and cross-corroborated it against a prior chat session that had already flagged the same WAL at 932MB two days ago -- it's grown 3.6x since with nothing fixed. Verified the backup/disk-exhaustion history via both code comments and verbatim prior-session chat transcripts (the 2026-09-10 97%-full incident and its fix). Found one new, live, unreported defect: nfl_qbr_weekly contains fabricated season-2026 data (copy-forward from 2025) for all 18 weeks, still unreplaced by real data as of this morning, actively feeding Week-1 fantasy/betting QB features right now. Verified two older reported issues against the live DB: the gsis_id crosswalk corruption is genuinely fixed, two ESPN leagues are still sync-failed exactly as before. Audited server/data/ lab dirs and pinpointed the exact market-lab duplicate (2 of 3 runs are byte-identical). Delivered a tiered cleanup plan respecting the hard rules and the app's own stated policy of never auto-pruning backups.
